sections.title: FOUNDATIONS OF INNER STRENGTH INSTITUTE
sections.bodyHtml: Heal. Grow. Perform. Belong. These foundations guide how Inner Strength Institute cares for clients and supports the people who make that care possible.

sections.title: WELCOME
sections.bodyHtml:
Welcome to Inner Strength Institute. Our work begins with a simple commitment: help people build the inner strength to meet life with greater resilience, connection and hope. We provide compassionate counseling for men, boys, athletes and everyone seeking a healthier, more fulfilling life.

Whether your role is clinical care, supervision, student training or practice support, you help create a respectful place where people can speak honestly and make meaningful progress. We value thoughtful judgment, clear communication, privacy and care grounded in evidence.

This handbook explains how we work together. Use its contents, search and handbook assistant to find the current policy, and follow the linked sections in Workplace Handbook Updates when a policy changes. Forms, records, evaluations and timekeeping belong in the app. Welcome to the team.

sections.title: PURPOSE AND BACKGROUND OF INNER STRENGTH INSTITUTE
sections.bodyHtml:
Inner Strength Institute brings together compassionate mental health care and a belief in each person’s capacity to grow. Its public-facing message—Stronger People. Brighter Tomorrows.—expresses the purpose behind our counseling practice.

The practice focuses on the pressures people carry: identity, relationships, anxiety, mood, performance and life transitions. Our website highlights men, boys and athletes while welcoming everyone on the journey toward a healthier, more resilient life.

Heal, Grow, Perform and Belong describe a connected approach to care. We help clients work through distress, develop insight, meet challenges with confidence and build meaningful connection. Counseling follows the client’s needs, goals and clinical treatment plan.

Our workplace puts that purpose into practice through confidential care, evidence-informed treatment, supportive supervision and a structured clinical student training program.

sections.title: VISION
sections.bodyHtml: Stronger people. Brighter tomorrows. We envision a community where seeking support is a sign of strength and people can access counseling that helps them live with greater resilience, purpose and connection.

sections.title: MISSION
sections.bodyHtml: To provide compassionate, evidence-informed counseling that helps people heal, grow, navigate pressure and build lasting inner strength—within a respectful, inclusive space where they can belong.

sections.title: GOALS
sections.bodyHtml:
1. Make the path into counseling clear, welcoming and responsive to each client’s needs.
  2. Provide individualized care for anxiety, stress, mood, relationships, identity and life transitions.
  3. Support men, boys and athletes with an understanding of pressure, performance and belonging, while welcoming all clients.
  4. Strengthen clinical judgment through supervision, reflection, evidence-informed practice and student training.
  5. Protect privacy, document care accurately and use the app consistently for workplace records.
  6. Support a sustainable workplace through clear expectations, fair compensation and respectful communication.

sections.title: VALUES
sections.bodyHtml:
Heal

Meet distress with compassion, safety and care that respects each person’s story.

Grow

Stay curious, welcome feedback and help clients and colleagues build insight and resilience.

Perform

Support healthy confidence and meaningful progress in life and performance, grounded in the person’s own goals.

Belong

Create an inclusive environment where people feel respected, heard and connected.

Clinical Integrity

Use evidence-informed methods, sound judgment and honest documentation within our authorized scope.

Confidentiality

Protect privacy and use client information only for authorized care and operations.

Shared Responsibility

Communicate clearly, follow through on commitments and seek support when a situation needs another perspective.

sections.title: PROFESSIONAL CONDUCT
sections.bodyHtml:
Harrassment

At Inner Strength Institute, we are committed to maintaining a workplace that is free of harassment. We will not tolerate any form of harassment, including bullying, offensive comments or conduct, and discrimination. Harassment can be based on various attributes such as race, color, religion, sex (encompassing sexual harassment and pregnancy discrimination), sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age (40 years and over), genetic information, or disability (whether physical or mental).

Furthermore, we strictly prohibit retaliation against individuals who report harassment, serve as witnesses, participate in the Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) process, or oppose any form of discrimination and harassment. Harassing conduct that negatively impacts an individual’s employment, work performance, or creates an intimidating, hostile, or offensive work environment will not be permitted. Employees are encouraged to report any instances of harassment promptly to their direct supervisor and/or People Operations People Operations, and we ensure a thorough and confidential investigation process, with appropriate corrective action taken when necessary.

Discrimination

Inner Strength Institute is dedicated to providing equal employment opportunities and fostering an inclusive environment, free from discrimination. We uphold a strict policy against discrimination on the basis of race, color, religion (creed), gender, gender expression, age, national origin (ancestry), disability, marital status, sexual orientation, or military status in any of our activities, operations, or employment practices.

We ensure that all employment decisions are based solely on an individual’s qualifications and ability to perform the essential functions of their job, without regard to any protected characteristics. We encourage all employees to report instances of discrimination to their direct supervisor and/or People Operations People Operations, and we are committed to taking appropriate disciplinary action, up to and including immediate termination, against any employee found to be in violation of this policy. There will be no retaliation against employees who file a complaint or participate in an investigation.

Honesty and Integrity in Self-Reporting

Providers are entrusted with the responsibility to report missed sessions, mileage, and outreach activities accurately and honestly.

This policy underscores the organization's commitment to high ethical standards. Providers are expected to adhere to principles of honesty and integrity in all self-reporting activities.

Auditing and Monitoring:

The organization reserves the right to conduct routine or random audits of self-reported data to ensure compliance and accuracy.

Audits may involve reviewing clinician reports, cross-referencing with other records, and, if necessary, seeking clarification or additional documentation from the clinician.

Providers will be informed about the audit process and what it entails, ensuring transparency in organizational practices.

Addressing Discrepancies:

Any discrepancies or inconsistencies identified during audits will be thoroughly investigated.

Providers will be given an opportunity to clarify any discrepancies in their reports before any action is taken.

Consequences of Intentional Misreporting:

The organization maintains a zero-tolerance policy towards intentional misreporting or fraudulent behavior.

Providers found to have purposefully or consistently provided inaccurate information in their self-reports are subject to disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment.

Depending on the severity and nature of the misconduct, legal actions may be pursued in addition to employment termination.

Providers are expected to commit to ethical conduct in all their professional activities, reflecting the values of honesty and integrity championed by the organization.

A process of Remediation (see “Remediation” for additional information) will be initiated if any audits identify misconduct or or inaccuracies in reporting.

Managerial and Supervisory Conduct

If you manage employees, you are responsible for your team members’ performance. To conduct effective regular meetings and performance evaluations, we expect you to:

Set clear objectives:

Your team members should know what you expect of them. When you first hire someone to your team, ensure they understand their job duties. Set specific goals for each team member (and team-wide if applicable.) Revisit those goals during quarterly performance reviews.

Provide useful feedback:

During scheduled meetings with your team members, give them both guidance and praise, as appropriate. Be fair and specific to help them understand and implement your feedback.

Keep your team members involved:

There should be two-way communication between you and your team. Make your expectations clear, but always take your team members’ motivations and aspirations into account. Discuss training and development opportunities that may interest your team members.

Keep logs:

With important incidents about each one of your team members, keeping logs will help you evaluate your team, but may also prove useful when rewarding, promoting or terminating your team members.

Professionalism and Responsible Use of Technology

Dress Code:

Our company’s official dress code is business casual. However, an employee’s position may also inform how they should dress. If you frequently meet with clients or prospects, please conform to a more formal dress code. We expect you to be clean when coming to work and avoid wearing clothes that are unprofessional (e.g. workout clothes).

As long as you conform with our guidelines above, we don’t have specific expectations about what types of clothes or accessories you should wear.

We also respect and permit grooming styles, clothing and accessories that are dictated by religious beliefs, ethnicity or disability.

Pets in the Workplace:

We love four legged friends. Please inform management and your client/s if you intend to bring an animal to the workplace. Obtaining written permission is necessary due to the potential of risk.

Remember, not all individuals are accepting of four-legged friends including, but not limited to, allergies, past trauma events, potential disturbances (barking), or any form of anxiety. The owner accepts all risk and any individuals utilizing pets in the workplace abide by requests of clients, co-workers, management, or building management for the removal of pets.

Internet Usage:

Our corporate internet connection is primarily for business. You must not use our internet connection to:

  • Download or upload obscene, offensive or illegal material.
  • Send confidential information to unauthorized recipients.
  • Invade another person’s privacy and gain access to sensitive information.
  • Download or upload pirated movies, music, material or software.
  • Visit potentially dangerous websites that can compromise our network and computers’ safety.
  • Perform unauthorized or illegal actions, like hacking, fraud or buying/selling illegal goods.
Email Usage:

No matter how you use your corporate email, we expect you to avoid:

  • Signing up for illegal, unreliable, disreputable or suspect websites and services.
  • Sending unauthorized marketing content or emails.
  • Registering for a competitor’s services, unless authorized.
  • Sending insulting or discriminatory messages and content.
  • Spamming other people’s emails, including your coworkers.
Cell Phone Usage:

We allow the use of cell phones at work. But, we also want to ensure that your devices won’t distract you from your work or disrupt our workplace. We ask you to follow a few simple rules:

  • Use your cell phone in a manner that benefits your work (business calls, productivity apps, calendars.)
  • Keep personal calls brief and use an empty meeting room or common area so as not to disturb your colleagues or clients.
  • Avoid playing games on your phone or texting excessively in public or shared service spaces.
  • Don’t use your phone for any reason while driving a company vehicle, if applicable.
  • Don’t use your phone to record confidential information.
  • Don’t download or upload inappropriate, illegal or obscene material using our corporate internet connection.
  • Phones are not allowed in restrooms.

Inner Strength Institute reserves the right to access and review electronic files, messages, internet use, emails, voicemails, and other digital archives. We reserve the right to monitor the use of electronic communications as necessary to ensure no misuse or violation of Inner Strength Institute policy or law.

Secure workplace communication

Use authorized app records, assigned tasks and secure communication workflows. Respect each person’s notification and texting preferences. Healthcare communications rollout requires the executed BAA for the covered services and the required safeguards, consent and testing; do not assume that signing a BAA makes every ordinary SMS exchange protected.

The app is the workplace system of record. Complete internal forms, requests, scheduling, clinical documentation, supervision records, evaluations, timekeeping and payroll submissions in the app. Use the appropriate record or assigned workflow; do not submit parallel Google Forms, external time logs, spreadsheets or emailed timesheets.

Record actual service and work time, review tracked entries, and submit missing time or corrections through the app. A missing tracking option does not make work unpaid. If a needed workflow is unavailable, report the issue through in-app support so the record can be completed or corrected.

Use authorized in-app communication and respect notification and texting preferences. Protect confidential information and use only approved recipient and access settings. Quick View access requires an individual protected code and a secure device. Emergency calls and required external reports must not be delayed while completing an app record; document the actions in the app as soon as it is safe.

Use App records, forms and timekeeping for app communication and record procedures.

sections.title: Business cards and public profiles
sections.bodyHtml:
You can print your own Inner Strength Institute business cards at the office. Preprinted cardstock with the Inner Strength Institute website QR code will be available, so you can print your provider information on the other side.

How to print
  1. Check your profile first. Open your public provider profile from the Provider Update and make sure your name, credentials, photo, contact information, and profile link are correct.
  2. Open the business card template in the app and use the current version.
  3. Get the cardstock. Preprinted business-card cardstock is located in the right drawer of the kitchen desk.
  4. Use the color Brother printer on the back side of the kitchen desk. The printer can only take one sheet at a time.
  5. Load the cardstock with the QR-code side facing up so the QR code is readable when you look at it.
  6. In the printer settings, set Print Quality to Great instead of Good and Paper Type to Matte Photo Paper. Click OK.
  7. Print one sheet first. Check that your information is correct and everything is properly aligned before printing additional cards.
  8. Once the test sheet looks correct, print additional sheets one at a time.

The preprinted QR code links to the main Inner Strength Institute website. If needed, the cards can also be printed on both sides.

Please use the current app-generated template and do not add a private care-texting number or other personal contact information that is not intended for public use.

If your profile information is incorrect or you have trouble with the template, printer, or alignment, use Need help in the Provider Update to submit a Technology support ticket before continuing. You can attach screenshots. General Inner Strength Institute support: the Support Team through the app.

sections.title: CODE OF CONDUCT & ACCOUNTABILITY
sections.bodyHtml:
Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Measures

Commitment to Fair Discipline:

Inner Strength Institute is committed to a fair and transparent disciplinary process. Disciplinary actions will be taken based on the specific circumstances of each case and may range from verbal warnings to termination. The following process will generally be followed:

  1. Verbal Warning: The employee will be informed verbally of the issue and expected to make improvements.
  2. Written Warning and Meeting: If the issue persists, a written warning will be issued, and a meeting will be held to discuss the next steps. At this stage, remediation and a probationary period may be initiated, though this is not required.
  3. Termination: If issues continue after the written warning, termination may be the final step.
Probationary Period:

Once probation has been initiated, any repeat offenses after the probationary period will result in step 2 (written warning and meeting) being the first step in the disciplinary process.

Illustrative List of Inappropriate Conduct:

The following list provides examples of conduct deemed inappropriate by Inner Strength Institute, though this is not an exhaustive list, nor does it limit Inner Strength Institute’s right to impose discipline for any other conduct it deems inappropriate:

  • Dishonesty
  • Falsification of company records
  • Unethical conduct in the production or handling of medical records
  • HIPAA violations
  • Unauthorized use or possession of property belonging to Inner Strength Institute, a coworker, or the public
  • Possession or control of illegal drugs, weapons, or explosives
  • Engaging in violence, threats of violence, use of vulgar or abusive language, horseplay, practical jokes, or disorderly conduct that may endanger others or damage property
  • Insubordination, failure to perform assigned duties, or failure to comply with Inner Strength Institute’s health, safety, or other rules
  • Unauthorized or careless use of Inner Strength Institute’s materials, equipment, or property
  • Unauthorized and/or excessive absenteeism or tardiness
  • Lack of teamwork, poor communication, or unsatisfactory performance
  • Sexual or other illegal harassment or discrimination
  • Unauthorized use or disclosure of Inner Strength Institute’s confidential information
  • Violations of any company policy
Confidentiality in Disciplinary Actions:

Inner Strength Institute is committed to upholding the privacy and dignity of all employees in disciplinary matters. Specific details of disciplinary actions will be kept confidential and will not be disclosed to the reporting party or any unauthorized individuals.

The organization ensures transparent communication with all parties involved, informing the reporting party that the matter has been addressed in line with Inner Strength Institute’s policies and procedures, thereby building trust and assurance.

Reporting Unethical Conduct and DORA:

Inner Strength Institute adheres to a strict policy for following all guidelines of reporting unethical conduct to DORA, the Department of Regulatory Agencies (and any other necessary governing bodies). Should an employee perform a reportable offense, Inner Strength Institute will not delay in their obligation to reporting such information should an internal audit produce such information. For a list of reportable offenses, please access the Department of Regulatory Agency’s website.

Inner Strength Institute will also abide by all regulations and investigations initiated by DORA (or other governing bodies) should they be conducted with any of Inner Strength Institute’s staff, past or present.

Remediation

In the event that any audit, investigation, or report highlights potential unethical conduct, misconduct, or behaviors misaligned with Inner Strength Institute’s vision and culture, a structured Remediation Process will be initiated.

The primary goal is to foster open communication regarding expectations of conduct and behavior, focusing on correcting and guiding rather than penalizing.

Remediation is a process aimed at addressing and correcting specific issues or actions. Minor infractions may involve informal corrective requests, e.g., a supervisor’s note in the app’s clinical record to modify the format of a clinical note. For more significant concerns, a formal ‘Notification of Remediation’ will be issued through the app, potentially accompanied by a ‘Contract of Remediation’.

Remediation is corrective, not punitive. It is not a reprimand. While the focus is on correction, individuals have the right to submit a ‘Remediation Reply’ within 48 hours through the app to provide additional information or context to People Operations in the app. This reply will be reviewed by the People Operations team; however, the generation and receipt of such a reply does not guarantee alterations to the notification or contract, if applicable.

This process is in alignment with legal and ethical standards and maintains strict confidentiality. It is distinct from processes initiated by external governing bodies.

Process of Remediation

Notification of Remediation

Initiation/Escalation: Administration, Manager/Supervisor, or Director issues a Notification of Remediation through the app to initiate the process.

Details:
  • This notification may or may not accompany a contract which must be signed by the employee/student/contractor.
  • This notification will include necessary information regarding the reason for remediation or “Areas of Concern”.
  • This notification will detail the expectations of the employee/student/contractor.
  • The notification may include any findings of audit or other potential investigation or reports.
Additional Expectations:
  • Depending on the level of severity, remediation may also correspond with reprimand, though remediation itself is not considered reprimand.
  • Depending on the level of severity, remediation may include information or stipulations regarding non-compliance (see “Non-Compliance of Remediation”).
Steps of Remediation
  • Step 1: Receipt of notification.
  • Step 2: Timely response to the notification (if necessary).
  • Step 3: Mandatory attendance to the remediation meeting (if necessary).
  • Step 4: Signature and agreement upon contractual remediation plan (if applicable).
  • Step 5: Non-compliance stipulations (if applicable).
Remediation Contract
  • The contract will detail the findings associated with the initiation or escalation of remediation or “Areas of Concern”.
  • This contract will include desired outcomes and expectations, including information of successful completion of the remediation plan.
  • This contract will include stipulations and information regarding the non-compliance of remediation.
Non-Compliance of Remediation

Details of non-compliance and consequences will be part of the Remediation Contract.

Recognizes that each case is unique and the contract will reflect specific expectations tailored to the situation.

Conflict Resolution, Reporting, and Safety Policy

Encouraging Open Dialogue:

This organization values a harmonious and respectful work environment. We believe that many issues can be resolved through open and honest communication. Therefore, we encourage all employees to address their concerns or disagreements directly with the colleague involved as a first step. This approach aims to foster a culture of understanding, empathy, and mutual respect.

Employees are encouraged to document their attempts at resolving the issue, noting the date, time, and a brief description of the conversation. This documentation is not required to be submitted to Inner Strength Institute but should be retained by the employee for their records.

Seeking Support and Escalation:

In cases of harassment, discrimination, or witnessing such behavior, employees are required to report the conduct immediately to their supervisor or People Operations through People Operations. It is crucial not to let an inappropriate situation continue by not reporting it.

Consistent with our commitment to a safe workplace, employees are expected to report all unsafe working conditions, accidents, and injuries, no matter how minor, as part of their responsibility to promote safety in the workplace.

Inner Strength Institute assures all employees that bringing forth a concern will not result in any form of retaliation. We are committed to ensuring a safe and supportive work environment for all.

Emphasizing Apology and Forgiveness:

This organization believes in the power of apologies and forgiveness as fundamental to resolving conflicts and maintaining a positive work environment. Employees are encouraged to be open to giving and receiving apologies and to engage in constructive dialogue aimed at reconciliation.

Acknowledging Irreversible Actions:

We recognize that certain actions and words, once expressed, cannot be taken back and may leave a lasting impact. Inner Strength Institute is committed to fostering an environment where such instances are acknowledged openly and addressed sincerely.

A genuine apology, expressed with sincerity and a commitment to change, holds significant value in mending relationships and rebuilding trust. We believe that in situations where no laws have been broken and no unethical behavior has been committed, an apology can serve as an appropriate and sufficient resolution.

While we uphold accountability, we also acknowledge that not every incident requires punitive measures. Management will exercise discretion in determining the most suitable response to each unique situation, always with the intention of upholding the dignity of all parties involved and maintaining the integrity of our workplace.

Inner Strength Institute is committed to creating an environment that encourages learning from mistakes and personal growth. We believe in providing opportunities for education and reflection, fostering a culture of continuous improvement.

Commitment to Fair and Prompt Resolution:

Inner Strength Institute is committed to addressing all concerns promptly and fairly. We have established procedures to investigate and resolve reported issues, ensuring that every employee’s voice is heard and valued.

This policy is part of our ongoing commitment to creating and maintaining a respectful and inclusive work environment. We welcome feedback from our employees on how we can continually improve our conflict resolution processes.

Inner Strength Institute is steadfast in its commitment to providing a safe workplace, emphasizing “safety first.” Employees play a critical role in this commitment and are expected to work in a safe manner, actively contributing to the maintenance of a secure work environment.

sections.title: WORKPLACE SAFETY & WELL-BEING
sections.bodyHtml:
Promoting a Safe and Respectful Workplace

Workplace Violence Policy:

Violence in our workplace is a serious form of harassment. It includes physical and sexual assault, destruction of property, threats to harm a person or property and verbal and psychological abuse. We want to avoid those incidents altogether, but we also want to be ready to respond if needed.

For this reason, we ask you to report to Legal (Legal) if you suspect or know someone is being violent. We will investigate the incident. We will treat employees who verbally threaten others as high risk and they will receive an appropriate penalty.

Violence as Speech:

Inner Strength Institute maintains a zero-tolerance policy for any form of violence, including violence expressed through speech. Violent speech encompasses any communication, whether verbal or written, that is intended to cause harm, intimidation, or fear.

We recognize the importance of understanding the intent behind words and actions. Intent to cause harm is a critical factor in determining the severity of an offense and the appropriate response. Deliberate and malicious intent to harm or demean another individual is unacceptable and will not be tolerated.

Promoting Respectful Communication:

Employees are encouraged to communicate with positive intent, seeking to understand and be understood, and to resolve conflicts in a respectful and constructive manner.

Employees have a responsibility to speak up against violent speech and to report any instances of such behavior to their supervisor, People Operations, or through established reporting channels.

Investigating Reports of Violent Speech:

All reports of violent speech will be taken seriously and will be thoroughly investigated. Inner Strength Institute is committed to ensuring a fair and unbiased investigation process.

In investigating reports of violent speech, the context in which the words were spoken, the impact on the individuals involved, and the intent behind the words will all be carefully considered.

Inner Strength Institute will take appropriate actions based on the findings of the investigation, which may include disciplinary measures, counseling, or other supportive interventions. Our goal is to address the issue comprehensively, ensuring the safety and well-being of all employees.

Substance-Free Workplace

We are a smoke free, drug free, and alcohol free workplace. Whether you are an employee, contractor or visitor, you must not bring, use, give away or sell any drugs on company premises. If you are caught with illegal drugs, or show that you are under the influence of substances, you will face disciplinary action up to and including termination. Employees may consume alcohol outside of work and in moderation at company sponsored events.

Contagious Illnesses

If an employee exhibits symptoms indicative of a contagious disease, such as vomiting, diarrhea, persistent cough producing mucus, fever, sore throat, enlarged lymph nodes, nausea, or chills, they are urged to take proactive measures to prevent transmitting the illness to both clients and colleagues. Promptly inform your direct supervisor of your condition to facilitate the consideration of temporary accommodations. This could involve shifting in-person sessions to virtual meetings, arranging for a substitute colleague if feasible and appropriate, or assisting in the rescheduling of appointments with clients. Your cooperation is crucial in maintaining a healthy and safe work environment.

sections.title: INCLUSION, RESPECT, AND COMMUNITY PERSPECTIVES
sections.bodyHtml:
Commitment to Fairness and Organizational Neutrality

At Inner Strength Institute, we are committed to fostering a professional environment grounded in fairness, neutrality, and mutual respect. Our community is enriched by a wide range of beliefs, values, backgrounds, and lived experiences, and we expect all individuals to engage with one another in a manner that upholds dignity, integrity, and equal opportunity.

Inner Strength Institute does not prioritize, elevate, or institutionally endorse any particular belief system, identity, ideology, or social group over another. This principle is essential to maintaining an environment where clients, families, and staff from diverse backgrounds feel equally welcomed, respected, and supported. Our focus remains on the quality of care provided, professional conduct, and the actions and contributions of each individual—not on symbolic representation or personal affiliation.

We believe that respect within our organization is earned through professionalism, accountability, and commitment to ethical practice. Differences in values or beliefs may exist, but they must not result in biased treatment, preferential consideration, or exclusion.

Personal Expression, Shared Spaces, and Professional Fit

Inner Strength Institute recognizes that individual staff members may hold personal beliefs, values, or affiliations and may choose to express these within their own private or individually assigned workspaces. Personal expression in a private office is permitted, provided it remains professional and does not interfere with service delivery, client care, or workplace functioning.

In shared workspaces, clinical environments, or areas used by multiple staff members or clients, personal displays or materials should be removed when the space is no longer exclusively in use by the individual. This practice helps maintain a neutral and inclusive environment and ensures that shared spaces are not perceived as representing the views, priorities, or endorsements of the organization or of any single group.

During clinical supervision and everyday interactions, differing viewpoints will naturally arise. These moments can be valuable opportunities for growth and learning when approached with professionalism, respect, and openness. Diverse perspectives may coexist without resulting in biased treatment, exclusion, or preferential consideration.

Clients retain the right to choose their providers in alignment with their needs and preferences, reflecting our commitment to client-centered care. We support a range of therapeutic approaches and professional perspectives, even when they differ from our own, provided they align with ethical standards, scope of practice, and organizational expectations.

All members of the Inner Strength Institute community are expected to reflect on their comfort engaging in a professional environment that values neutrality and the presence of differing beliefs. If an individual finds it challenging to function within a setting that does not center or promote specific identities, values, or viewpoints, Inner Strength Institute may not be the appropriate workplace for them.

Our goal is to cultivate a workplace where fairness, professionalism, and mutual respect guide our interactions. We encourage thoughtful dialogue, continuous learning, and accountability as we work together in service of effective, ethical, and client-centered mental health care.

sections.title: CONFIDENTIALITY AND PRIVACY
sections.bodyHtml:
Confidentiality and Privacy

We want to ensure that private information about clients, employees, partners and our company is well-protected. Examples of confidential information are:

  • Employee records
  • Unpublished financial information
  • Data of customers/partners/vendors
  • Customer lists (existing and prospective)
  • Unpublished goals, forecasts and initiatives marked as confidential

As part of our hiring process, we may ask you to sign non-compete and non-disclosure agreements (NDAs.) We are also committed to:

  • Restrict and monitor access to sensitive data.
  • Develop transparent data collection procedures.
  • Train employees in online privacy and security measures.
  • Build secure networks to protect online data from cyberattacks.
  • Establish data protection practices (e.g. secure locks, data encryption, frequent backups, access authorization.)

We also expect you to act responsibly when handling confidential information.

You must:

  • Lock or secure confidential information at all times.
  • Shred confidential documents when they’re no longer needed.
  • Make sure you view confidential information on secure devices only.
  • Only disclose information to other employees when it’s necessary and authorized.
  • Keep confidential documents inside our company’s premises unless it’s absolutely necessary to move them.

You must not:

  • Use confidential information for your personal benefit or profit.
  • Disclose confidential information to anyone outside of our company.
  • Replicate confidential documents and files and store them on insecure devices.

This policy is important for our company’s legality and reputation. We will terminate any employee who breaches our confidentiality guidelines for personal profit. We will pursue legal action within the law.

We may also discipline any unintentional breach of this policy depending on its frequency and seriousness. We will terminate employees who repeatedly disregard this policy, even when they do so unintentionally.

Legal Matters and Subpoenas

Inner Strength Institute prioritizes the privacy of our students and the integrity of the therapeutic process. To protect our staff and the individuals we serve, the following protocols must be followed regarding legal matters:

  • If a clinician or staff member is served with a subpoena, court order, or request for production of documents, they must not acknowledge or release any information immediately. All legal documents must be forwarded to the Inner Strength Institute Director of Operations and Administration (Michael Mendez) within 24 hours.
  • All requests for medical documentation (Progress Notes, Treatment Plans, Summaries) must follow the established Inner Strength Institute administrative "train." Clinicians are not permitted to hand-deliver or email records directly to attorneys or the courts. All documentation must be vetted by Admin to ensure only the "minimum necessary" information is shared.
  • No records will be released without a valid, HIPAA-compliant written authorization from the client (or legal guardian) or a specific court order signed by a judge. A subpoena alone is often insufficient for the release of sensitive mental health records under Colorado law.
  • Under no circumstances should staff discuss case details with outside legal counsel without prior approval from Inner Strength Institute Administration.

sections.bodyHtml:
Purpose

Inner Strength Institute (“ISI”) is committed to maintaining a safe environment for all employees, clients, and visitors. This policy outlines procedures for addressing potential safety risks, emergency situations, and specific incidents that may occur in a counseling setting.

Scope

This policy applies to all employees, interns, contractors, and volunteers at ISI.

Complete safety and incident records in the app. Immediate danger requires an emergency response first; do not delay calling 911 or making required reports while completing documentation.

sections.title: Office kiosk and client arrivals
sections.bodyHtml:
The new office kiosk brings client check-in and office information together in one place.

  • Client check-in: Clients select their provider and appointment time, confirm who is checking in, and let the provider know they have arrived. If an appointment is missing, they can use “Message our support team” or ask the office team for help.
  • Arrival notifications: The kiosk records the client’s arrival and sends an in-app notification to the provider. Depending on notification settings, text or email alerts may also be available. Check the app for arrivals.
  • Today’s providers: View provider office hours and room information.
  • Office directory: Find rooms and view the office layout.
  • Provider profiles: View current provider photos and public profile information. Please keep your photo, biography, and focus areas up to date through your Provider Update.
  • Programs & events: View available office programs and events. Program-specific check-in or clock-in/out options will only appear where configured.
  • Visit forms & feedback: Complete assigned visit questionnaires or feedback after check-in. Optional feedback can be skipped and will not prevent check-in. Authorized providers can review saved responses and available trends.

The kiosk will return to the welcome screen after completion or inactivity. Please finish or clear the screen before leaving it and let staff know if any information appears incorrect.

The kiosk is intended for arrival and office information only. It is not used to start care or report an emergency.

Staff can open the configured office kiosk; clients should use the device provided at their office.

sections.title: GENERAL SAFETY PROCEDURES
sections.bodyHtml:
Building Access & Security

Employees must keep entrance doors locked unless actively admitting scheduled clients.

If you notice a door is unlocked and no staff member is present (or scheduled to be present), lock the door and immediately contact your direct supervisor and/or the ISI main number.

Employees are to wear or carry identification (e.g., name badge) when on the premises, if provided.

Authorized Personnel & Visitors

All visitors must have a legitimate reason for being on-site (e.g., a scheduled appointment or official business).

Staff should greet visitors and clients in the reception area and record arrival through the app’s appropriate check-in workflow.

Unknown or Suspicious Individuals (“Strangers”)

If someone you do not recognize is in the building without a clear reason:

Politely ask if you can assist them.

If they refuse to identify themselves or become agitated, do not engage further— immediately notify your direct supervisor or call the main number for assistance.

If you feel unsafe or threatened, call 911.

sections.title: IF AN EMPLOYEE ENCOUNTERS AN UNLOCKED, UNATTENDED BUILDING
sections.bodyHtml:
Verify Schedules

Check staff schedules (in the app’s schedule) to confirm no one is expected to be on-site.

Secure the Premises

Lock all doors and ensure all windows are secure.

Notify Management

Text or call your direct supervisor and/or the ISI main number to report the situation.

If there are indications of forced entry or suspicious activity, contact 911 before leaving the site.

sections.title: CLIENT ELOPEMENT PROCEDURE
sections.bodyHtml:
Respond according to the client’s age, consent, clinical risk and approved care plan. Parent or guardian notification applies where that person is authorized to receive it. An adult’s departure is not by itself permission to restrain the person or disclose confidential information. Seek clinical leadership guidance and emergency help when there is immediate danger.

In a counseling context, “elopement” generally refers to a minor or at-risk client unexpectedly leaving the premises without permission.

Immediate Response

Attempt to ensure client safety first. If the client is still within sight, calmly encourage them to remain on-site or return to the building.

If the client flees or refuses to return, do not leave other clients unattended to chase after them. Instead, contact your supervisor or call the main office for support.

When a Parent/Guardian IS Present

Advise the parent/guardian to follow or contact their child if appropriate.

Gather relevant information about the incident (time, direction, child’s appearance, any known triggers or safety concerns).

Document the incident and actions taken in the app.

When a Parent/Guardian is NOT Present

Attempt to contact the parent/guardian immediately.

If the client is a minor and the parent/guardian cannot be reached, notify your direct supervisor. The supervisor will decide whether law enforcement or another emergency contact is necessary.

Document the incident thoroughly in the app.

sections.title: NO-SHOW PARENT PICK-UP PROCEDURE
sections.bodyHtml:
The pickup procedure applies to children and clients whose approved care arrangement requires release to an authorized caregiver. Confirm the applicable consent and release arrangements in the client’s app record.

Waiting Period

If a minor client’s parent/guardian does not arrive at the scheduled pick-up time, attempt to contact them immediately (phone, text).

Keep the child in a safe, supervised area until they are picked up.

Escalation

If you cannot reach the parent/guardian within 15–30 minutes (or per state guidelines), notify your direct supervisor.

The supervisor may advise contacting local authorities or Child Protective Services (CPS) if there is a pattern of abandonment or a concerning lack of response.

Documentation

Record in the app the time you began calling the parent/guardian and the attempts made to reach them.

Document in the app any instructions or next steps given by your supervisor or authorities.

sections.title: CRISIS SITUATIONS: SUICIDAL OR HOMICIDAL IDEATION
sections.bodyHtml:
Assess Immediacy of Danger

If a client expresses imminent risk to self or others (e.g., has a plan, means, and intent), call 911 or the local crisis line immediately.

If the risk seems urgent but not imminent, contact your direct supervisor or the ISI main number for guidance.

Contact Supervisor/Clinical Lead

Text or call your direct supervisor, or use the main ISI administrative support line:

Provide essential details (e.g., client initials, risk assessment, immediate concerns).

Follow directives given by your supervisor or on-call clinical lead.

Safety Plan & Documentation

Develop or update a safety plan with the client (and guardian if applicable).

Thoroughly document the incident in the app, including any steps taken, resources provided, and persons contacted.

Mandatory Reporting

If there is a concern about abuse, neglect, or a credible threat of harm, report to the appropriate authorities in line with mandatory reporting obligations.

sections.title: COMMUNICATION & EMERGENCY CONTACT PROTOCOL
sections.bodyHtml:
Primary Contact Methods

For routine requests, contact your direct supervisor through the app. For an urgent safety concern, call the supervisor or main office; use only approved communication methods for confidential details.

ISI main number: use the current office contact information supplied by ISI Administration for business-hours support.

For a scheduled after-hours service, confirm the designated supervisor or clinical lead and their current contact information with ISI Administration before the service.

Escalation Steps

Attempt to contact your direct supervisor.

If the supervisor is unavailable, contact the ISI main number or next available manager.

If there is immediate danger to life or property, call 911 first, then inform your supervisor at the earliest safe opportunity.

sections.title: TRAINING & REVIEW
sections.bodyHtml:
Employee Training

All new hires receive an orientation on this Workplace Safety Policy.

Existing staff must review and acknowledge the policy in the app at least annually, or when significant updates are made.

Policy Updates

ISI reserves the right to update this policy as needed. Changes will be communicated promptly to all employees.

sections.title: App records, forms and timekeeping
sections.bodyHtml:
The app is the workplace system of record. Complete internal forms, requests, scheduling, clinical documentation, supervision records, evaluations, timekeeping and payroll submissions in the app. Use the appropriate record or assigned workflow; do not submit parallel Google Forms, external time logs, spreadsheets or emailed timesheets.

Record actual service and work time, review tracked entries, and submit missing time or corrections through the app. A missing tracking option does not make work unpaid. If a needed workflow is unavailable, report the issue through in-app support so the record can be completed or corrected.

Use authorized in-app communication and respect notification and texting preferences. Protect confidential information and use only approved recipient and access settings. Quick View access requires an individual protected code and a secure device. Emergency calls and required external reports must not be delayed while completing an app record; document the actions in the app as soon as it is safe.

sections.title: WORKFORCE CLASSIFICATIONS AND CONDITIONS
sections.bodyHtml: At Inner Strength Institute, we value the contributions of our team members and recognize the need for clear employment classifications. This section outlines the various staffing categories within our organization, including hourly employees, fee-for-service providers, salaried employees, and temporary staff, as well as clarifications regarding full-time, part-time, and independent contractor status. Each classification has distinct expectations, work hours, and general benefit eligibility. For more information regarding compensation, paid-time-off, benefits, and specific policies related to your classification, please refer to the corresponding sections of this handbook.

sections.title: WORKFORCE CLASSIFICATIONS
sections.bodyHtml:
Inner Strength Institute recognizes that different roles within the organization require different employment structures, compensation models, and expectations. This section defines the primary workforce classifications used by the Practice based on the nature of the employment relationship and method of compensation. Each classification carries distinct expectations related to scheduling, service delivery format, documentation responsibility, and eligibility for compensation and benefits.

Specific role expectations, scope of practice, supervision requirements, service authorization, and clinical responsibilities are governed by the applicable Role-Based Practice Expectations, Career Pathways, and other relevant sections of this Workplace Handbook, as well as the individual employment agreement.

Hourly Employees (Indirect Service):

Hourly indirect-service employees do not provide direct client services. These employees support the organization through operational, administrative, coordination, training, or program support functions. Compensation is provided at a single hourly rate determined by role and responsibilities, as outlined in the applicable employment agreement and compensation policies.

Hourly Employees (Direct Service or Dual Roles):

Hourly direct-service or dual-role employees provide direct services, or a combination of direct and indirect services, and are compensated on an hourly basis. Hourly rates may vary depending on the type of service performed (e.g., direct service versus indirect service), as defined by applicable compensation and payroll policies. Authorization to provide specific services is determined by role assignment, credentialing status, supervision requirements, and program approval.

Fee-for-Service Providers (Direct Service):

Fee-for-service providers are compensated based on approved services rendered rather than hours worked. Compensation is tied to service delivery, documentation accuracy, and compliance with payer and Practice requirements, as outlined in the applicable employment or provider agreement. Fee-for-service arrangements may be modified or discontinued at the Practice’s discretion, subject to applicable agreements and handbook policies.

Salary Employees (Indirect Service):

Salary indirect-service employees do not perform direct client services and are compensated through a fixed salary. These roles typically include leadership, management, coordination, supervision, administrative, or operational functions. Performance expectations and responsibilities are defined by role and outlined in the employment agreement and applicable handbook sections.

Salary Employees (Direct Service or Dual Roles):

Salary direct-service or dual-role employees perform direct services or a combination of direct and indirect responsibilities and are compensated through a fixed salary structure. Service expectations, including minimum averages or thresholds for direct services, are defined by role and outlined in the employment agreement and applicable compensation policies.

All salary employees with direct-service expectations are expected to maintain schedule availability exceeding minimum service requirements by approximately twenty-five percent (25%) to account for cancellations, no-shows, and scheduling variability.

Practicum/Intern Students:

Individuals enrolled in an approved practicum or internship program through an academic institution may participate in Inner Strength Institute’s Student Training Program. Practicum students and interns are classified separately from employees for purposes of compensation and benefits eligibility. Specific expectations, supervision requirements, service limitations, and compensation (if applicable) are governed by the Student Training Program section of this Handbook and the applicable training or affiliation agreement.

Contractors:

Contractors operate as self-employed individuals or entities and are not considered employees of Inner Strength Institute. Contractor relationships are governed by separate written agreements defining scope of work, compensation, duration, and deliverables. Contractors are expected to comply with applicable Practice policies necessary for service delivery but are not eligible for employee benefits.

Temporary Employees:

Temporary employees are hired for interim coverage, seasonal programming, or project-based needs. Employment is of limited duration and may conclude prior to the anticipated end date based on operational needs, funding availability, or program changes.

Full-time, part-time and temporary status

For non-clinical staff, full-time classification is at least 40 hours per week or an average of 150 hours per month; part-time is fewer than 40 hours per week. For clinical staff, full-time classification is at least 25 service credits per week; part-time is fewer than 25 credits per week. Service credits are not a substitute for actual work-time records.

Each person is advised of their classification and appointment duration at hire. A temporary assignment has a limited duration. A full-time or part-time label does not by itself establish benefit eligibility; the individual agreement and current benefits framework govern. Clinical authority, service eligibility and pay remain subject to the current role and compensation policies.

sections.title: CONDITIONS OF EMPLOYMENT
sections.bodyHtml:
Employment Status and Duration

Employees may be hired on a full-time or part-time basis under temporary or indefinite arrangements. Employment status, role designation, and any applicable contractual terms are communicated at the time of hire and may change based on organizational needs, funding, performance, or program requirements.

Eligibility for compensation and benefits is governed by the individual employment agreement, assigned role, and the Benefits section of this Workplace Handbook.

At-Will Employment

Employment with Inner Strength Institute is at-will. Either the employee or the Practice may terminate the employment relationship at any time, with or without cause or notice, consistent with applicable law. Nothing in this Handbook alters the at-will nature of employment unless explicitly stated in a written agreement signed by both parties.

Background Checks and Ongoing Eligibility

All employees must successfully complete required background checks prior to commencing work with clients or accessing client information. Continued employment may be contingent upon maintaining eligibility consistent with program, regulatory, payer, and contractual requirements. Employees are expected to promptly disclose any information that may affect background clearance, credentialing, or service eligibility.

Certifications and Legal Requirements

Employees must obtain and maintain all certifications, clearances, and legal requirements necessary to perform their assigned role. Failure to maintain required certifications or clearances may result in changes to duties, suspension of services, or separation from employment.

Training and Professional Development

Employees are expected to complete required onboarding, compliance training, program-specific instruction, and professional development within designated timeframes. Failure to complete required training may impact scheduling, service eligibility, or continued employment.

Ethical and Legal Disclosures

Employees must promptly disclose any ethical, legal, licensing, or regulatory matters that may affect their ability to perform assigned duties or provide services. Disclosures must be made in accordance with Practice policy and applicable law.

Compliance with Policies

Continued employment with Inner Strength Institute is contingent upon compliance with all applicable policies contained in this Workplace Handbook. Failure to comply may result in corrective action, up to and including termination of employment.

Ownership of Records and Materials

All client records, documentation, data, and materials created or accessed in the course of employment are the exclusive property of Inner Strength Institute. Access is granted solely for the performance of assigned duties and must be relinquished upon separation from employment.

sections.title: CAREER PATHWAYS, JOB TITLES, SERVICE FOCUS AND COMPENSATION STRUCTURE
sections.bodyHtml:
Inner Strength Institute utilizes structured career pathways to define job titles, role progression, and default compensation structures across clinical and clinical support roles. Career pathways are designed to promote clarity, consistency, transparency, and professional development while maintaining flexibility to meet programmatic, regulatory, and operational needs.

Placement within a career pathway is determined by a combination of education, credentials, licensure or certification status, experience, supervision requirements, assigned Service Focus, and organizational need. Advancement within or between pathways is not automatic and may require management review and approval.

This section establishes career tiers, job titles, levels, and default compensation reference rates only.

Role-specific authority, scope of practice, supervision obligations, documentation standards, and service limitations are governed by the Role-Based Practice Expectations section of this Handbook and applicable agreements.

Nothing in this section constitutes a guarantee of compensation, promotion, advancement, hours, or continued employment.

sections.title: CAREER PATHWAY OVERVIEW
sections.bodyHtml:
Inner Strength Institute career pathways are organized into three tiers, with Tier 3 representing the highest level of clinical responsibility and advancement:

  • Tier 1: Practice Support Track
  • Tier 2: Pre-Licensed / Unlicensed Master’s Track
  • Tier 3: Licensed Clinical Track

Each tier includes five levels reflecting increasing responsibility, experience, and leadership capacity within the tier’s authorized scope.

TIER 1: Practice Support Track

Practice support roles assist with access, scheduling, records and care coordination within the assigned role. This track does not authorize independent counseling or clinical billing. Individual titles and duties follow the written role assignment. The shared category and level compensation schedule remains applicable to the assigned work.

TIER 2: Pre-Licensed / Unlicensed Master’s Track

Focus: Advanced Clinical Service Provision (Licensed or Unlicensed)

This tier applies to individuals holding a Master’s degree in a mental health–related field who are authorized to provide services under applicable supervision, credentialing, and program requirements. Licensure pursuit may or may not be required depending on role and program assignment.

Authorization to provide services is determined by credentialing status, supervision requirements, payer rules, and program approval—not solely by licensure intent.

Job Titles (Tier 2):
  • Level 1: Associate Therapist I
  • Level 2: Associate Therapist II
  • Level 3: Advanced Associate
  • Level 4: Senior Associate
  • Level 5: Principal Associate
Compensation schedule

Career-track titles do not set a separate hourly pay schedule. Use CATEGORY AND LEVEL COMPENSATION RATE SCHEDULE and the employee’s assigned compensation category, level, service eligibility, and individual agreement.

Optional Licensure Transition

Individuals who later obtain full licensure may be eligible for transition to Tier 3 at a level determined by the Practice. Transition is not automatic and does not guarantee promotion or compensation adjustment.

TIER 3: Licensed Clinical Track

Focus: Clinical Autonomy and Leadership

This tier applies to fully licensed clinicians providing therapeutic services within their licensed scope of practice and, at advanced levels, contributing to supervision, mentorship, and program oversight.

Job Titles (Tier 3):
  • Level 1: Staff Clinician I
  • Level 2: Staff Clinician II
  • Level 3: Senior Clinician
  • Level 4: Lead Clinician
  • Level 5: Principal Clinician
Compensation schedule

Career-track titles do not set a separate hourly pay schedule. Use CATEGORY AND LEVEL COMPENSATION RATE SCHEDULE and the employee’s assigned compensation category, level, service eligibility, and individual agreement.

sections.title: SERVICE FOCUS ASSIGNMENT
sections.bodyHtml:
Inner Strength Institute is a counseling-only practice. Services include authorized individual counseling, adolescent counseling, family-related clinical care, and counseling for anxiety, stress, depression, life transitions and performance-related concerns. Clinical assessment, treatment planning and necessary care coordination support those services.

Care occurs in approved offices or through approved telehealth. A service assignment does not expand credentials, supervision or payer authorization. Sports and performance support is counseling within the provider’s clinical scope; it does not establish a separate instructional or non-clinical program.

sections.title: CATEGORY AND LEVEL COMPENSATION RATE SCHEDULE
sections.bodyHtml:
Category and level rate schedule

Clinical Hour Rate
The assigned credit value multiplied by your clinical rate. This covers approved 9-series clinical codes and designated master’s-level services in the appendix; it does not authorize every code beginning with 9. A 1.00-credit service pays the full rate and a 0.75-credit service pays 75%. Routine administrative work is included in this service pay. The 1.20 equivalent affects sick-leave accrual, not additional cash pay.
Standard Professional Rate
The rate used to calculate the Direct Service component of an Integrated Service from the service-specific minutes, units, or time-equivalent. The included indirect allowance is 20% of that direct time-equivalent, paid at the applicable Indirect Service Rate, unless the Compensation Schedule specifies another allowance.
Indirect Service Rate
The hourly rate used for the included indirect component and separately compensable qualifying Indirect Service. Do not submit the same included work twice. Qualifying excess work remains reportable and payable.
Support activity pay
The hourly rate for designated support activities, including required Provider Update review. Record actual compensable time.
Probationary and minimum-workload rates
Two distinct conditions that use the stated reduced rate: new-hire probation and the minimum-workload policy. Each has its own timing and exceptions, as described in the current Introductory Compensation and Minimum Workload Rate policies. A slash in the prior chart separated H-code and clinical rates; it did not combine them into one payment.
Levels and conditional bonuses
A compensation level selects the base rate within the credential category; it is separate from a workload/benefit tier. The chart’s “+” amount is conditional, not guaranteed and not included in base pay. The addition applies only when the employee qualifies for Tier 3 based on sessions per pay period.
Conditional Tier 3 additions

Tier 3 currently requires 50 qualifying session credits per two-week pay period. Current-period session credits determine this addition; retained benefit tiers during grace do not qualify.

This addition is conditional compensation governed by the current, effective Workplace Handbook schedule for your category and level; it is separate from your agreed base rate. Inner Strength Institute may change or discontinue the addition, its eligibility criteria or the categories and levels that receive it prospectively, with notice before affected work. If the handbook no longer provides an addition for your category and level, the addition ends on that change’s effective date, even if you remain in Tier 3. Earned additions for earlier work remain payable under the policy then in effect.

Record changes in the app’s pay-system rate settings with their prospective effective date and give staff notice. Changing handbook prose alone does not recalculate payroll.

Spanish-language pay differential

The differential is governed by 23. Spanish Language Proficiency Differential. It requires an approved course, successful certificate, verified eligibility, and qualifying Spanish-language Direct Services. Tier 2 adds $1 and Tier 3 adds $2 per qualifying Workload Clinical Hour; Tier 1 has no differential. It does not increase indirect or support rates.

sections.title: COMPENSATION AUTHORITY AND MODIFICATION
sections.bodyHtml:
Beginning on this amendment’s effective date, I will be compensated at the applicable rates in my individual compensation schedule for the services and duties I perform, regardless of the payment or funding source. This includes insurance, self-pay, grants, iMatter and other externally funded programs or contracts. My compensation is based on the approved service, credits or hours and assigned duties, rather than a percentage of the amount billed, collected or reimbursed. For work covered by this amendment, these terms replace prior funding-specific percentage or revenue-sharing compensation arrangements. Applicable approved differentials and separately stated role or duty rates continue to apply. This change applies prospectively after the required signatures and does not reduce compensation already earned.

Rationale

Funding arrangements have changed over time, and some external contracts have omitted provider-compensation terms or applied them inconsistently. Using each employee’s agreed service and duty rates provides a consistent basis for compensation across programs. Differences in a program’s reimbursement do not create an automatic increase or decrease in the employee’s rate.

For example, a covered 1.00-credit clinical service pays the employee’s agreed per-credit rate whether funded by insurance, a grant or iMatter. It is not paid as 50% of a program’s reimbursement under this amendment. Salaried employees remain subject to their salary agreements. Approved supervision, mentoring and other assigned-duty rates remain governed by the employee’s individual schedule. Any separate group-work compensation must be agreed in writing under the group-review policy.

Payroll must retain the prior arrangement for earlier service dates and apply the new method only from the completed amendment’s prospective effective date. Editing the handbook alone does not change an existing signed agreement or activate a percentage-pay override.

sections.title: DEFINITION OF SERVICES
sections.bodyHtml:
For purposes of this Agreement and all related policies, a “Service” refers to an activity performed by a Provider on behalf of Inner Strength Institute that falls within the scope of authorized clinical, support, or outreach functions and is delivered in accordance with applicable laws, payer requirements, credentialing standards, and Inner Strength Institute policies and procedures.

Services are generally categorized as Direct Services, Indirect Services, or Outreach Services, as described below. Not all services are billable, and compensation is determined by the Provider’s individual contract, assigned role, and applicable policies.

sections.title: Indirect Services
sections.bodyHtml:
Definition and Purpose

Indirect Services consist of non-client-facing activities that are necessary to support the delivery, authorization, documentation, or coordination of approved Direct Clinical Services. Indirect Services exist solely to enable effective, compliant Direct Service delivery and are expected to be limited in scope and duration.

This policy applies to employees whose duties are primarily direct service. Employees in approved dual-role or administrative positions may have additional indirect responsibilities as defined by their role, assignment, or contract.

Indirect Services are not billable to third-party payers and are compensated only as permitted by the individual’s contract and applicable Inner Strength Institute policies.

Authorized Indirect Services

Separately compensable Indirect Service is limited to qualifying client-care, client-acquisition, and coordination work under 13. Separately Compensated Indirect Service. Routine work already included in FFS or Integrated Service compensation is not paid twice. Required meetings, training, organizational work, and compensable assigned travel follow 14. Support Activity.

Limitations and Expectations

Work must be assigned or otherwise qualify under the applicable service and duty policy. Report all compensable work, including qualifying excess time, without duplicate payment. Approval or documentation concerns are addressed separately from earned wages.

Performance Standards

Employees whose duties are primarily Direct Services are expected to maintain an Indirect-to-Direct time ratio of 25% or less, with an agency target of 10–15%, consistent with Inner Strength Institute performance standards.

Indirect time may be reviewed and cross-referenced with documentation, audit logs, contract assignments, and productivity data.

Governing Authority

Use of Indirect Services is governed by:

  • This Workplace Handbook
  • The approved counseling coding and documentation procedures
  • Individual employment or contractor agreements

Where discrepancies exist, authorization and assignment requirements prevail.

sections.title: Typical Duties – Mental Health Counselor
sections.bodyHtml:
The duties listed below describe the typical responsibilities associated with the Mental Health Counselor role. These duties are provided for operational guidance and may vary based on licensure level, program assignment, client needs, and organizational priorities. This list is not exhaustive, and duties may be modified, expanded, or reassigned at the Practice’s discretion.

  • Provide individual counseling services to children and adolescents experiencing emotional, behavioral, or mental health concerns, including anxiety, depression, trauma-related symptoms, and emotional dysregulation.
  • Establish a safe, supportive therapeutic environment that fosters trust, emotional expression, and growth.
  • Support clients in identifying triggers, developing coping strategies, improving emotional regulation, and building resilience.
  • Assist clients in strengthening self-esteem, interpersonal skills, and stress management abilities.
  • Facilitate therapeutic small-group counseling sessions focused on emotional awareness, communication skills, peer relationships, and conflict resolution.
  • Lead psychoeducational discussions addressing topics such as emotional intelligence, coping with stress, self-advocacy, and healthy relationships.
  • Adapt group content and facilitation style to meet participants’ developmental and emotional needs.
  • Conduct clinical assessments and participate in the development of individualized treatment plans.
  • Establish measurable treatment goals aligned with client needs and clinical best practices.
  • Monitor client progress through documentation, behavioral observations, and client or caregiver self-reports.
  • Adjust therapeutic interventions based on progress data, clinical judgment, and supervision guidance.
  • Communicate appropriately with parents or guardians regarding treatment goals, progress, and recommendations, consistent with consent and confidentiality requirements.
  • Provide guidance and psychoeducation to families to support skill generalization outside of sessions.
  • Coordinate with authorized outside care and educational partners when clinically appropriate and within consent and confidentiality requirements. ISI services take place at approved ISI offices or through approved virtual care.
  • Complete all required clinical documentation accurately and within established timelines.
  • Adhere to ethical standards, confidentiality requirements, and applicable laws and regulations.
  • Maintain compliance with Practice policies, procedures, and clinical standards.
  • Participate in audits, reviews, or quality assurance activities as required.
  • Participate in required supervision, consultation, and training activities.
  • Seek feedback and guidance to support clinical growth and competency development.
  • Maintain appropriate licensure, certifications, and continuing education requirements as applicable.
  • Support program development, group initiatives, or specialized clinical offerings as assigned.
  • Assist with referrals, coordination of care, and resource identification when appropriate.
  • Perform other duties consistent with the Mental Health Counselor role as assigned by the Practice.

Service authorization and app records

These duties do not expand credentials or authorize diagnosis, counseling or insurance billing outside the person’s approved role. Complete session records, progress notes, required forms and actual-time reporting in the app.

Client group counseling requires express written approval under Group counseling authorization. An assigned counseling role does not independently authorize a new group.
