sections.title: PAID TIME OFF (PTO) AND SICK & PERSONAL CARE LEAVE POLICY
sections.bodyHtml:
Paid Time Off (PTO) is an umbrella term for separate leave categories. Protected Sick and Personal Care Leave, salaried Personal PTO, and Training PTO each follow their own eligibility, use, balance, and payment rules. Protected sick leave is not a vacation bank, and Training PTO is restricted to approved training.

PTO Submission

Employees must submit all Paid Time Off (PTO) requests through the company’s web application via “Submit” in “My Dashboard” at app.theinnerstrengthinstitute.com.

To request PTO:

  1. Login to app.theinnerstrengthinstitute.com
  2. Via “My Dashboard”, select the “Submit” card.
  3. Select “PTO”.
  4. Indicate the type of PTO requested (Sick and Personal Care Leave, Personal PTO, Training PTO) in accordance with your employment agreement.
  5. Enter the requested date(s) and any required details.
  6. Submit the form for review and approval.

Training PTO requests use My Payroll under the Training Leave policy below. Personal PTO requests follow operational approval; protected sick-leave requests follow the protected-use policy.

PTO Categories

Sick and Personal Care Leave

Protected paid sick leave is administered under Sick-leave accrual ratio for fee-for-service staff. It is separate from vacation or general Personal PTO. Preserve earned balances and more generous earned terms. It accrues without a probationary waiting period.

Personal PTO

Allotted paid time off for salaried employees, specified in individual employment agreements. Personal PTO may be used at the employee’s discretion, subject to accrual, probationary, and usage limitations outlined in this policy.

Training PTO

Training leave accrues at 0.25 hour per 30 qualifying hours or service-credit equivalents, using the same documented qualifying basis as sick leave. Use Training leave — separate from sick leave for eligibility, the 20-hour balance cap, payment, and requests in My Payroll. Required employer training remains paid work even without an available leave balance.

Tracking and Usage

People Operations maintains leave balances and confirms the ADP handoff without counting imported periods twice. Review balances and submit Training PTO requests in My Payroll. Protected sick-leave notice and documentation follow Sick-leave accrual ratio for fee-for-service staff. Training requests require a description and participation documentation as specified in Training leave — separate from sick leave.

Accrual and Eligibility by Classification

Hourly employees accrue protected sick leave based on actual qualifying work. FFS employees use Clinical Hours × 1.20 for the standard sick-leave time equivalent, and Integrated Services include compensated direct and included indirect time once. Include separately compensable work and reconcile required accrual against actual work. See Sick-leave accrual ratio for fee-for-service staff and 18. Sick Leave Time Equivalency.

Training leave uses the same qualifying basis, including eligible fee-for-service and salaried work, at 0.25 training hour per 30 qualifying hours or equivalents. Personal PTO for salaried employees remains as specified in the individual agreement. The supplied Personal PTO terms allow use after a 60-day probationary period, with up to 10% available during that period. These leave terms are separate from introductory compensation and do not delay protected sick leave.

Salary Employee PTO Adjustments

Personal PTO allocations and pro-ration follow the employee’s individual agreement and applicable protections. Preserve earned balances and more generous earned terms. Do not apply a general Personal PTO probation, deduction, or forfeiture rule to protected sick leave.

Rollover and Accrual Caps

Protected sick-leave carryover follows Sick-leave accrual ratio for fee-for-service staff; the former generic 10-hour rollover cap does not apply. The more generous 65-hour annual sick-leave accrual cap in this handbook remains in place. Preserve earned balances and required carryover. Training leave carries forward until used, pauses accrual at a 20-hour balance cap, and resumes after approved use.

Usage Limits and Emergency Use

Personal PTO scheduling follows the employee’s agreement and operational approval process. Requests for more than 15 consecutive hours of general Personal PTO require 30 days’ notice and management approval. Salaried direct-service providers may use Personal PTO to fill deficient contractual hours as provided in their agreements. Protected sick leave is not subject to a generic 15-hour consecutive-use cap, per-pay-period cap, or 30-day advance-notice rule. Apply the protected uses, reasonable notice, permitted documentation, and nonretaliation requirements in Sick-leave accrual ratio for fee-for-service staff.

Year-End Use

Schedule Personal PTO in accordance with the applicable agreement. Operational restrictions on general Personal PTO do not limit protected sick-leave use. Training leave retain their separate balance and use rules.

Termination Payout

Apply the employee’s agreement, applicable leave policy, and earned-balance protections to each bank separately. Preserve more generous earned terms and any required payout. Training PTO remains restricted to approved training. retains its earned-balance protections and must not be treated as forfeited sick leave.

Policy Modifications

Inner Strength Institute reserves the right to modify this policy at any time. Updates will be communicated to employees in a timely manner.

sections.title: Sick-leave accrual ratio for fee-for-service staff
sections.bodyHtml:
Initial ratio: 20% administrative equivalent

Clinical credits × 1.20 ÷ 30 = sick-leave hours earned. The direct bucket receives 1.00 equivalent hour per credit and the administrative bucket receives 0.20. Thus 25 credits = 30 equivalent hours = 1 hour of sick leave; 0.75 credit = 0.90 equivalent hour = 0.03 sick-leave hour. The administrative equivalent affects accrual only for psychotherapy credit services and is already included in service pay.

Integrated Direct Service time and its included Indirect Service time enter the accrual calculation once. Under the standard 20% allowance, one direct hour plus 0.20 included indirect hour equals 1.20 accrual hours. Do not apply another clinical-credit multiplier to that total. Separately compensated Indirect Service, Support Activity, and qualifying Excess Time also count without duplication. Reconcile against all actual compensable work and apply any required sick-leave shortfall.

This remains protected paid sick leave, not a new vacation bank. It accrues without a probation waiting period and is paid using the highest currently eligible rate under the sick-leave pay policy. Payroll applies the HFWA calculation rules for the leave dates, using the currently applicable clinical per-credit or direct hourly base rate, excluding Tier 3 additions and other bonuses or differentials. Preserve existing balances and more generous earned terms. HFWA generally requires at least one hour per 30 hours worked up to 48 annually, with applicable carryover up to 48 hours; protected uses, reasonable notice, permitted documentation and nonretaliation requirements apply. Do not apply a generic 10-hour rollover cap or 30-day notice rule to protected sick leave.

Inner Strength Institute may update the ratio prospectively through the dated handbook appendix and corresponding payroll policy version, with notice and any required agreement. Preserve accrued balances and historical service calculations. AI documentation does not change the ratio automatically or remove pay for required review and correction. Actual work remains compensable even with a zero allowance. Any separate vacation/general PTO entitlement retains its existing protections.

sections.title: Training leave — separate from sick leave
sections.bodyHtml:
Training PTO is paid time earned for approved professional development and training. All hours and service-credit equivalents that qualify for sick-leave accrual also qualify for training accrual, including fee-for-service and salaried employees’ eligible work. The rate is 0.25 training hour per 30 qualifying hours or credits. Use the same documented qualifying basis as sick leave, including applicable clinical-credit equivalents; do not add an equivalent twice.

Training PTO is restricted to approved training and may not be converted to general PTO. It pays at the employee’s applicable sick-leave payment rate for the use date. Required employer training remains paid work even if this benefit has no available balance.

Tracking, cap and ADP handoff

People Operations enters or confirms the current ADP training balance in the app, together with the last completed pay period included in that balance. The app then accrues subsequent eligible periods without counting imported hours again. Staff view their balance and requests in My Payroll. Unused training hours carry forward until used. Accrual pauses at a 20-hour balance cap and resumes after approved use; a cap does not erase an existing balance.

Requesting Training PTO

In My Payroll, choose Training PTO, enter the training date and hours, provide a brief description, enter the training cost and upload a receipt, signup confirmation or proof of participation. People Operations may request further participation documentation. Inner Strength Institute may deny a request if sufficient documentation is not provided. The balance is deducted only when payroll approves the request and applies its payment. Pending or denied requests do not reduce the earned balance. A separate expense reimbursement requires its own approval; reporting a course cost does not automatically create a second payment.

See Continuing Education in the Employee Benefits Overview for additional approval and reimbursement requirements. Training leave is separate from protected sick leave .

sections.title: Jury Duty Policy
sections.bodyHtml:
Inner Strength Institute supports employees in fulfilling their civic obligations and complies with Colorado’s jury duty compensation requirements. The key points of our policy are:

Payment Obligation

In accordance with Colorado law (C.R.S. 13-71-126), Inner Strength Institute will pay eligible employees their regular wage (up to $50 per day) for the first three days of jury service or any portion thereof.

If your regular daily pay is less than $50, you will receive your actual pay. If your regular daily pay exceeds $50, the maximum required by law is $50 per day.

Beyond Three Days of Service

If jury service extends beyond three days, any additional time off may be unpaid, unless otherwise specified by your employment contract or other company policies (e.g., you may elect to use accrued PTO to cover additional days, if you wish).

Salaried (Exempt) Employees

Salaried exempt employees will not have their regular weekly salary reduced for partial-week jury service. However, the daily $50 compensation cap set by law still applies to the first three days of actual jury duty (or your regular pay if lower).

Proof of Service

To keep proper records, employees called for jury duty must bring a copy of the court summons and any documentation confirming they served (e.g., juror attendance slips).

Scheduling & Notice

If you receive a jury summons, please inform your supervisor as soon as possible. Keep them updated regarding the length of your jury service and coordinate schedules accordingly.

Retaliation Prohibited

Inner Strength Institute will not discharge, harass, or otherwise penalize you for responding to a jury summons or serving on a jury, in compliance with Colorado law.

sections.title: Holiday Scheduling Policy
sections.bodyHtml:
Employee Classifications for Holiday Benefits

For the purposes of holiday scheduling and pay, staff are divided into two categories:

  • Service Providers (Clinicians): Staff providing direct client services in approved ISI service settings.
  • Administrative Staff: Non-service providers supporting business operations.

Service Provider Schedule (No Recognized Holidays)

Service Providers operate on a standard workweek regardless of recognized company holidays.

  • Caseload Expectations: There is no reduction in minimum caseload requirements during holiday weeks. Clinicians are expected to maintain their standard direct-service hour targets.
  • No Pre-Approval Required: Since these are standard workdays for clinicians, no prior approval is needed to see clients or perform administrative tasks on these days.
  • Pay: Work performed on these days is paid at the clinician’s standard rate (or fee-for-service equivalent) and does not trigger holiday incentive pay unless specifically authorized for a high-needs shift.

Administrative Staff Schedule (Recognized Holidays)

Administrative Staff follow the company’s recognized holiday calendar.

  • Holiday Pay: Administrative staff are not required to work on recognized holidays and will receive their regular daily pay for these dates.

sections.title: OVERTIME AND WORK LIFE BALANCE
sections.bodyHtml:
General Expectation:

We aim to prevent overtime by managing schedules and loads (including the fee-for-service 36 direct-hour cap as a scheduling control). Off-the-clock work is prohibited. All time worked must be recorded in the app. If work occurs, it will be paid in accordance with law; policy violations (e.g., working without approval) may be addressed separately through coaching/discipline. No retaliation will occur for accurately reporting hours worked.

Non-Exempt Employees:

  • Pre-approval required: Overtime must be approved in advance by a supervisor/People Operations.
  • If overtime happens (approved or not): The Company will pay for all hours worked, including any unauthorized overtime, and may address the policy violation separately.
How to record time:
  • Record all direct services, indirect/admin time, meetings, and other compensable time in the app.
  • Use the web application via “Submit” in “My Dashboard” at app.theinnerstrengthinstitute.com to report approved variances/excess time that legitimately exceed the Credit Schedule hour-equivalents, and for reimbursements. Approved variances feed the Pay Calculations section.

Overtime Calculation (Non-Exempt):

Overtime is owed for (a) hours over 40 in a workweek, (b) hours over 12 in a single day, or (c) 12 consecutive hours (whichever yields more overtime). The Company calculates the regular rate each workweek by dividing total remuneration by total hours worked (including time paid for direct services, indirect/admin/meetings, and any non-discretionary differentials allocated to that week). When multiple rates apply in a week (e.g., direct and indirect), the regular rate is a weighted average.

OT premium owed = 0.5 × regular rate × overtime hours (because straight time has already been paid at the applicable rates).

For fee-for-service roles without an hourly rate, the Role-Based Supplemental Compensation Rate Schedule supplies hourly equivalents used in the regular-rate calculation. Employees must record all time in the app and use the claim form to submit approved variances.

See Payroll & Compensation → Pay Calculations (Non-Exempt/FFS) for the weekly greater-of true-up (FFS vs. hourly-equivalent) methodology.

Exempt Employees:

Exempt staff do not receive overtime; however, they must meet duties and salary-level tests. Colorado’s 2025 minimum salary for most EAP exemptions is $1,086.25/week ($56,485/year). If an exempt employee does not meet the exemption tests, they are treated as non-exempt for overtime. Raise any persistent over-capacity concerns with your supervisor.

Dual-Role Employees:

If you perform both exempt and non-exempt work, track and report all hours. Non-exempt time is subject to the overtime rules above.

sections.title: MEAL AND BREAK PERIODS
sections.bodyHtml:
Lunch Break Policy:

All employees who work eight or more hours in a day are required to take an unpaid meal break between 30 and 60 minutes. Meal breaks are not counted toward hours worked. Employees are to be completely relieved from duty during their meal break. Employees who work over 10 hours are required to take at least two 30 minute breaks.

Rest Break Policy:

Rest breaks are to be no longer than 15 minutes. You are not required to take a break, but we encourage it for your health and well-being. Here’s how it works:

  • Breaks are offered 2 times a day for full time employees who work 6 hours or more daily.
  • They are offered only once a day for part time employees who work 5 hours or less daily.
  • Rest breaks are on the clock, meaning you don’t have to clock-out for a rest break.
  • Breaks can be taken any time after your first 2 hours on the job on a given workday.
  • Employees are to remain in the building or on the property during their rest break.
  • It is recommended employees use the break room rather than remain in the work area, so as not to cause a distraction to other workers not on break.
  • Please notify your supervisor when a rest break is needed to ensure work is covered while you’re on break.

While our break time policy is generous, breaks will be monitored to ensure that work does not suffer. Therefore, we reserve the right to discipline any employee found abusing our break time policy by, for example, taking too many breaks, taking breaks that are too long, and/or disturbing staff that are not on break.

sections.title: PAID FAMILY AND MEDICAL LEAVE (COLORADO EMPLOYEES)
sections.bodyHtml:
Beginning January 1, 2024, employees working in Colorado may be eligible for up to 12 weeks of wage-replacement benefits per year for Paid Family and Medical Leave from the state of Colorado.

Contributions and Eligibility:

Employees are generally required to contribute to the state-run Paid Family and Medical Leave program through payroll deductions, starting in 2023.

To be eligible for wage-replacement benefits, employees must meet certain wage-base requirements set by the state, follow administrative rules set by the state, and submit a request to the Colorado Division of Family of and Medical Leave Insurance (CDFMLI). The CDFMLI determines eligibility for and the amount of wage-replacement benefits.

Basic Leave Entitlement:

Beginning January 1, 2024, eligible employees may take up to 12 weeks of unpaid leave and may receive wage-replacement benefits based on what the employee has paid into the policy for the following reasons.

  • To care for their own serious health condition;
  • To care for a child during the first year after the birth, adoption, or placement through foster care of that child;
  • To care for a family member with a serious health condition;
  • Because of any qualifying exigency arising out of the fact that the employee’s family member is on active duty (or has been notified of an impending call or order to active duty) in the armed forces; and
  • When the employee or their family member is a victim of domestic violence, stalking, or sexual assault.

Note: Employees with a serious health condition related to pregnancy or childbirth complications may take up to an additional four weeks (16 weeks in total).

Under this policy, family member is defined as:

  • The employee’s child, spouse/domestic partner, parent, sibling, grandparent, grandchild;
  • The child, parent, sibling, grandparent, or grandchild of the employee’s spouse/domestic partner;
  • Any individual with whom the employee has a significant personal bond that is like a family relationship.

Intermittent Leave:

Employees may take leave under this policy intermittently, but wage-replacement benefits from the state won’t be payable until the employee accumulates at least 8 hours of benefits.

Employee Notice:

When the need for leave is foreseeable, employees must notify Inner Strength Institute through People Operations at least 30 days in advance. If the need for leave isn’t foreseeable, employees must provide as much leave as is practical.

Job Restoration:

Eligible employees returning from Paid Family and Medical Leave will generally be reinstated to the position they held before the start of the leave, or to a comparable position with comparable pay, benefits, and other terms and conditions of employment, provided they have been with Inner Strength Institute LLC for at least 180 days.

Benefits Continuation:

During the duration of Paid Family and Medical Leave, an employee’s existing health benefits will be maintained as if the employee had continued to work. The employee must continue to pay their portion of the costs for health benefits.

Relationship with Federal FMLA and Other Leave Policies:

Where applicable, when an employee's leave qualifies under the federal Family and Medical Leave Act (“FMLA”), the leave used counts against the employee's entitlement under both laws and must be taken concurrently. To the extent the Company offers the employee leave through another plan or policy, the plan or policy with the greatest protection will apply.

Anti-Retaliation:

Inner Strength Institute LLC will not retaliate against an employee for requesting or using leave under this policy.

sections.title: TIMEKEEPING, COMPENSATION, AND PAYROLL COMPLIANCE
sections.bodyHtml:
Timekeeping Policy:

This policy governs how all work time is recorded for payroll, billing integrity, and benefit eligibility. It applies to all Service Providers, Supervisors, and other staff who record time related to client care or program operations.

System of Record

Record clinical service documentation and actual service time in the app. Record Indirect Service, Support Activities, supervision, corrections and other compensable work in the app’s timekeeping and payroll workflows. Clinical credits and automatic allowances do not replace actual-time records.

Accurate time tracking in notes and all medical and non-medical documentation is mandatory. The duration entered must reflect the actual time spent providing the service or completing the administrative task.

Accuracy Requirement

Failure to enter accurate times (e.g., defaulting every session to the same length, inflating administrative time, or failing to enter indirect service) may result in:

  • Correction of entries,
  • Loss of Tier eligibility for benefits,
  • Denial of discretionary payments (e.g., missed session bonus), and/or
  • Corrective action up to and including termination.

Audit Rights

The Practice may audit entries using: (a) app timestamps (log-in, log-out, note signature), (b) claims and units billed, and (c) schedules.

Providers with a high percentage of “default” times or excessive administrative time may be selected for additional review.

Time Entry and Documentation Deadline

Each pay period concludes on Friday.

All sessions and required medical documentation must be entered into the app no later than 11:59 p.m. on the following Sunday.

Entries completed after this deadline may not be captured through standard payroll or billing processes.

Late-Added Sessions

Sessions entered or documented after 11:59 p.m. on the Sunday following the end of the pay period are considered late-added sessions.

Late-added sessions:

  • Are not automatically captured in payroll
  • Remain payable for compensable work; late documentation is handled separately from earned wages
  • Require a correction submission in the app for review

Late-added sessions must be submitted using the web application via “Submit” in “My Dashboard” at app.theinnerstrengthinstitute.com.

Required information includes the date of service, client initials, service code, duration, confirmation that documentation is complete in the app, and the reason for late entry.

Credit Cap Policy (Fee-for-Service Providers)

To ensure compliance with wage and hour laws, the Practice establishes a weekly credit cap for fee-for-service providers.

The 36-credit weekly limit is a scheduling control, not a conversion of credits into actual work hours. Record all actual work and report excess time; minimum-wage and overtime calculations follow the applicable day and workweek requirements.

Non-Service Provider Timekeeping

Non-service providers must track all working hours and submit accurate time records in the app by midnight on the Friday ending the pay period.

Non-exempt employees must record all hours worked and are prohibited from working off the clock. Any errors in time records must be promptly reported using the web application via “Submit” in “My Dashboard” at app.theinnerstrengthinstitute.com.

See Actual time, support activities and corrections for required work, missed tracking, review time, and supervision compensation. 15. Excess Time does not authorize averaging workweeks for overtime.

sections.title: Actual time, support activities and corrections
sections.bodyHtml:
The Workplace Handbook identifies activities eligible for indirect pay and support-activity pay. These activity types will be added to the web application as needed. Inner Strength Institute reserves the right to designate activities as indirect work or support activities and to add, revise or reclassify activity types prospectively. The applicable classification and rate will be communicated before the work is performed. Record actual compensable time under the designated activity; a missing app option should be reported for entry or correction. A later classification change does not reduce pay already earned or permit duplicate payment.

Record all compensable work daily. Provider Update active review time is tracked by session and section and submitted for payroll review at the applicable support activity rate. Paused, hidden and timed-out periods are not automatically credited; report legitimate unrecorded work through a correction request. Actual work beyond an allowance remains compensable.

Clinical credits and automatic indirect equivalents are not substitutes for actual time records. Apply applicable minimum wage, overtime, rest-period and regular-rate rules, including workweek and daily requirements. A late note, missing preapproval or denied claim does not erase earned wages. Handle documentation or approval concerns separately from paying for work performed.

Clinical supervision compensation

Clinical supervision is paid at the supervisor’s individually negotiated or contracted hourly rate. This handbook does not set a universal supervision dollar rate.

Assigned responsibilityCompensation basis
Direct clinical supervision100% of the contracted supervision hourly rate
Hosting group clinical supervision150% of the contracted supervision hourly rate

sections.title: BENEFITS TIER FRAMEWORK:
sections.bodyHtml:
The Practice uses a three-tier system to determine eligibility for benefits and certain forms of discretionary compensation. Tiers are based on each provider’s average direct and indirect service credits/hours, calculated over rolling payroll periods.

This framework ensures fairness, transparency, and consistency across all programs and benefit categories.

Tier Levels:

Out of Compliance (Below Tier 1)

Indicates insufficient average credits/hours to qualify for Tier 1.

Employees in this category do not qualify for optional tier-funded benefits during the applicable period. Earned wages, protected leave, earned balances, and legally required benefits or reimbursements remain protected.

Employees who remain Out of Compliance for more than six (6) pay periods in a calendar year may be subject to review and corrective action, up to and including reassignment of duties, adjustment of employment classification, or termination.

New employees are in their Grace Period for the first 90 days, six pay periods, or until they reach Tier 1—whichever comes first.

Tier 1 – Entry Level

Limited Practice-funded benefits.

Employees remain eligible for reduced or minimal benefits.

6-12 direct service hours per week.

Tier 2 – Standard Level

Eligible for partial or moderate Practice-funded benefits.

13-24 direct service hours per week.

Tier 3 – Premium Level

Eligible for the highest level of Practice-funded benefits.

25 direct service hours per week and up.

Note: The exact benefits attached to each Tier vary by benefit category (e.g., insurance, supervision, childcare, PTO accrual). Some benefits are scaled by percentage, while others are scaled by frequency or coverage limits.

How Tiers Are Measured:

Measurement Window:

Calculations are based on a rolling bi-weekly average of direct credits (total credits for fee-for-service providers), then converted into a weekly average.

Direct service hours count toward Tier calculation only when the session note is completed within the documentation deadline for that pay period.

Payroll Tracker Access:

Employees may review their tier, qualifying credits, grace status, and pay calculations in My Payroll and request corrections.

Each line displays:

  • Current Window: Tier assignment + bi-weekly average; weekly average; rolling sum.
  • Example: “Tier 2 (29.0 bi-wk avg; 14.5/wk; sum 58.0)”
  • Previous Window: Same format for the prior period.
  • Status: “Grace” (if tier dropped and grace is active), “Current” (if stable or improved), or “Out of Compliance” (if below Tier 1).

If a period has no data (0.00 or blank), the cell may be blank instead of displaying “Out of Compliance.”

Grace Period:
  • If an employee’s Tier drops, a one-pay-period grace period applies.
  • If performance recovers within the grace window, benefits remain unchanged.
  • If performance does not recover, benefits will be adjusted to the corresponding lower Tier.

Application of Tiers:

Discretionary tier-based benefits, reimbursements, and conditional compensation follow their applicable tier rules.

Below Tier 1 means no optional tier-funded benefit for that period, subject to applicable grace and exemption rules; earned wages, protected leave, earned balances, and legally required reimbursement remain protected.

Some benefits scale by percentage (e.g., insurance contributions, missed session pay, mileage reimbursement).

Other benefits scale by frequency or coverage (e.g., number of supervision sessions per month, number of childcare hours, PTO accrual patterns).

Each benefit’s scaling rules are described in its respective section of the Handbook.

Intern Classification:

Interns are classified separately from employees and providers for purposes of benefits eligibility. Unless expressly stated otherwise in a written agreement, interns are not eligible for Practice-sponsored benefits, reimbursements, or Tier-based compensation programs. The Benefit Tier Framework applies only to eligible employees and providers.

Protected sick leave, earned wages, and earned leave balances are governed by their applicable policies; being below a discretionary benefit tier does not remove those protections. Minimum-workload service rates and the Tier 3 lookback exemption are governed by 20. Minimum Workload Rate and 21. Tier 3 Minimum Workload Exemption.

Supervision:

Supervision is a valued benefit provided through our Clinical Development Program, designed to support your professional growth and enhance clinical competencies. Whether pursuing licensure or seeking ongoing professional development, our structured supervision and training opportunities are available at no cost or with compensated participation as applicable. For more detailed information, please refer to the Supervision Policy.

Liability and Clinical Malpractice Insurance:

The Practice provides liability insurance and clinical malpractice insurance for its authorized operations, including authorized clinical work performed by employees and clinical students/interns. This handbook does not extend coverage to unrelated outside activities or promise coverage for work performed before joining the Practice. Request a certificate of insurance or clarification of coverage from People Operations through the app.

Continuing Education

Approved professional development may use Training leave — separate from sick leave. Eligible work uses the same qualifying accrual basis as sick leave. Required employer training remains compensable work, even when no Training PTO balance is available.

A course cost does not automatically create reimbursement. A separately approved reimbursement follows its applicable policy, including 23. Spanish Language Proficiency Differential. Benefit-tier changes follow the one-pay-period grace rule in BENEFITS TIER FRAMEWORK:.

sections.title: Health Insurance — employee-only employer contribution

sections.title: Increased Self-Pay Rates
sections.bodyHtml:
Eligible Providers may request approval to increase their self-pay rates subject to the conditions below. Rate adjustments may be requested no more frequently than once per calendar quarter and require prior approval.

Eligibility & Approval

  • Requests must be initiated by the Provider through the Support Team or Administrative Staff.
  • Approval may require review by the Provider’s supervisor, site lead (if applicable), Clinical Director (if applicable), and/or Administrative Staff.
  • Approval is discretionary and may be granted or denied based on operational, clinical, or administrative considerations.

Client Communication Requirements

  • Providers may elect to apply the new rate to existing self-pay clients or establish a grandfathered rate for current clients.
  • Clients must receive full disclosure of the rate change and be given the opportunity to decline services and seek an alternative Provider.
  • Increased self-pay rates may not be combined with or billed to insurance.
  • All client communications related to rate changes are the responsibility of the Provider.

Providers acknowledge that changes to self-pay rates may result in a reduction in caseload or scheduling and assume all associated risks.

Compensation Structure

For services covered by the completed amendment, compensation uses the employee’s individual service and duty rates regardless of funding source. Prior self-pay percentage and revenue-sharing arrangements are replaced prospectively. A client charge or collected upcharge does not itself create a percentage payment to the provider. Apply historical terms to earlier service dates and honor approved written duty rates under COMPENSATION AUTHORITY AND MODIFICATION.

Applicable Services

Increased self-pay rates most commonly apply to 90837 (Individual Psychotherapy, 53–74 minutes).

Alternative service codes may be considered with approval.

Billing Protocol

Record the actual service duration and use the approved service code consistent with the service, documentation, and payer or self-pay requirements. A fee amount does not authorize submitting a shorter-duration code regardless of the service delivered. Use Service codes: Clinical Session Rate and Direct Care Rate and the Compensation Schedule for the applicable compensation value.

sections.title: Nights and Weekends Self-Pay Upcharge (99051)

sections.title: CLINICAL COMPENSATION, INTEGRATED SERVICES, TIME EQUIVALENCY & ADDITIONAL COMPENSATION POLICY
sections.bodyHtml:
Purpose

This policy establishes the Practice's operational framework for:

  • Fee-for-Service Clinical Hour compensation;
  • Integrated Service Compensation;
  • per-minute and fixed service calculations;
  • included routine administrative compensation;
  • separately compensable Indirect Service;
  • Support Activities;
  • Excess Time;
  • Sick Leave time equivalencies;
  • Workload Clinical Hours;
  • Minimum Workload Rate administration;
  • regional and language differentials; and
  • related payroll and timekeeping requirements.

The Practice utilizes more than one compensation methodology because professional services vary in duration, billing structure, administrative burden, credentialing requirements, reimbursement methodology, and the ability to reliably identify actual service minutes.

The compensation method applicable to a service is established in the Practice's current Compensation Schedule.

sections.title: 1. Employee Service Compensation Eligibility
sections.bodyHtml:
Employees may be designated as:

Bundled / Integrated Service Only

The Employee is eligible to provide approved services compensated through the Practice's Integrated Service Compensation methodology but is not credentialed or authorized to provide services compensated through the FFS Clinical Hour methodology.

FFS Eligible

The Employee is credentialed and authorized to provide qualifying Fee-for-Service Clinical Hour Services.

FFS-eligible Employees may also provide Integrated Services.

FFS eligibility does not mean that every service performed by the Employee is compensated through the Clinical Hour methodology.

The compensation method assigned to the service controls.

sections.title: 2. Primary Compensation Methods
sections.bodyHtml:
The Practice utilizes two primary service-compensation methods:

A. Fee-for-Service Clinical Hour Services

Qualifying professional services are assigned a defined Clinical Hour Value and compensated according to the Employee's applicable Clinical Hour Rate.

B. Integrated Service Compensation

Integrated Services provide compensation for:

  • a Direct Service Component; and
  • an Included Indirect Service Component.

Integrated Services may be calculated using:

  • actual qualifying service minutes;
  • units;
  • a fixed encounter value;
  • predetermined Direct Service minutes;
  • a Direct Service time-equivalent; or
  • another service-specific methodology established by the Compensation Schedule.

Unless otherwise identified by the Practice:

  • qualifying 9-series professional/CPT services are compensated through the FFS Clinical Hour methodology when performed by an eligible Employee; and
  • qualifying H-code services are compensated through Integrated Service Compensation.

The Compensation Schedule controls when a service-specific exception applies.

sections.title: 3. Clinical Hour
sections.bodyHtml:
A Clinical Hour is the Practice's standardized service-value unit used to assign compensation and measure qualifying clinical workload.

A Clinical Hour is not a clock hour.

The Clinical Hour assigned to a service does not necessarily correspond to the exact number of minutes required to perform that service.

A qualifying service may be assigned:

  • 0.25 Clinical Hour;
  • 0.50 Clinical Hour;
  • 0.75 Clinical Hour;
  • 1.00 Clinical Hour;
  • 1.50 Clinical Hours;
  • 2.00 Clinical Hours; or
  • another value established by the Compensation Schedule.

Clinical Hour Values may reflect:

  • service requirements;
  • typical clinical responsibility;
  • administrative requirements;
  • complexity;
  • reimbursement structure;
  • operational considerations; and
  • other relevant factors.

The duration of a billing code alone does not determine its Clinical Hour Value.

sections.title: 4. Clinical Hour Rate
sections.bodyHtml:
Each FFS-eligible Employee is assigned an applicable Clinical Hour Rate.

Compensation is calculated as:

Clinical Hour Value × Clinical Hour Rate = Service Compensation

For example, where the Employee's Clinical Hour Rate is $44.00:

The Clinical Hour Rate is a fee-for-service rate, not a general hourly wage for every clock hour worked.

A service assigned 0.50 Clinical Hour therefore earns 0.50 of the applicable Clinical Hour Rate even when the actual duration of that individual service differs from 30 minutes, subject to the Excess Time and wage-compliance provisions of this policy.

sections.title: 5. FFS Standard Time Equivalent
sections.bodyHtml:
Each Clinical Hour also carries a Standard Time Equivalent for administrative and time-equivalency purposes.

Unless otherwise specified:

1.00 Clinical Hour = 1.20 Standard Time Equivalent Hours

or:

1.00 Clinical Hour = 72 Standard Time Equivalent Minutes

The proportional equivalents are:

Clinical Hour ValueStandard Time Equivalent
0.250.30 hours / 18 minutes
0.500.60 hours / 36 minutes
0.750.90 hours / 54 minutes
1.001.20 hours / 72 minutes
1.501.80 hours / 108 minutes
2.002.40 hours / 144 minutes

The Standard Time Equivalent does not multiply the Employee's Clinical Hour Rate.

For example:

1.00 Clinical Hour at a $44 Clinical Hour Rate = $44.00 in FFS compensation.

The corresponding 1.20 Standard Time Equivalent Hours are used separately for applicable administrative, Sick Leave, and Excess Time calculations.

sections.title: 6. Routine Work Included in FFS Compensation
sections.bodyHtml:
FFS Clinical Hour compensation is intended to compensate the qualifying clinical service together with the ordinary work directly associated with completing that service.

Routine included responsibilities may include:

  • preparation;
  • review of immediately relevant clinical information;
  • routine clinical documentation;
  • progress-note completion;
  • routine chart review;
  • brief client or guardian follow-up;
  • routine scheduling associated with the service;
  • brief authorized care-team or provider communication;
  • ordinary care coordination;
  • routine documentation corrections; and
  • other ordinary administrative responsibilities directly associated with completion of the compensated service.

FFS Employees do not separately submit routine administrative time already contemplated by the Clinical Hour compensation structure and its Standard Time Equivalent.

sections.title: 7. Integrated Service Compensation
sections.bodyHtml:
Integrated Service Compensation replaces the Practice's former general Direct Service hourly methodology for applicable services.

An Integrated Service generally consists of:

Direct Service Compensation + Included Indirect Service Compensation

Unless the Compensation Schedule establishes another allowance:

Included Indirect Service Time = 20% of compensated Direct Service Time

Accordingly:

60 Direct Minutes = 12 Included Indirect Minutes

The Direct Service Component and Included Indirect Service Component are calculated separately using the applicable rates.

sections.title: 8. Integrated Direct Service Component
sections.bodyHtml:
Each Employee performing Integrated Services is assigned an applicable Standard Professional Rate used to calculate the Direct Service portion of those services.

The Direct Service Component may be based upon:

  • actual documented Direct Service minutes;
  • predetermined Direct Service minutes;
  • units;
  • a fixed encounter value;
  • a defined Direct Service time-equivalent; or
  • another methodology identified in the Compensation Schedule.

Use of an hourly-equivalent calculation rate does not make the Employee a general hourly Direct Service employee.

The rate is used to calculate the Direct Service portion of the Integrated Service payment.

sections.title: 9. Included Indirect Service Component
sections.bodyHtml:
Integrated Services also include compensation for ordinary administrative responsibilities associated with the service.

Unless otherwise specified:

Included Indirect Service Time = Direct Service Time × 20%

The Included Indirect Service Component is compensated using the Employee's applicable Indirect Service Rate.

Examples:

Direct ServiceIncluded Indirect
15 minutes3 minutes
30 minutes6 minutes
45 minutes9 minutes
60 minutes12 minutes
90 minutes18 minutes

The allowance is intended to recognize ordinary administrative responsibilities associated with completing the service.

It does not require the Employee to spend precisely the allotted amount of time performing administrative work.

sections.title: 10. Per-Minute Integrated Services
sections.bodyHtml:
Certain Integrated Services are compensated according to actual documented Direct Service minutes.

For these services:

Actual Direct Minutes ÷ 60 × Applicable Standard Professional Rate = Direct Service Compensation

The Included Indirect Service allowance is then calculated as:

Actual Direct Minutes × 20%

and compensated using the applicable Indirect Service Rate.

Example

If:

  • Standard Professional Rate = $32.00 per 60 minutes;
  • Indirect Service Rate = $24.00 per hour; and
  • Direct Service = 15 minutes;
  • then:

Direct Compensation

15 ÷ 60 × $32.00 = $8.00

Included Indirect Time

15 × 20% = 3 minutes

Included Indirect Compensation

3 ÷ 60 × $24.00 = $1.20

Total Integrated Service Compensation = $9.20

The Employee does not separately submit the first three routine Indirect minutes because compensation for that ordinary administrative allowance is already included in the service payment.

sections.title: 11. Fixed, Unit-Based, and Per-Encounter Integrated Services
sections.bodyHtml:
Certain services may be compensated using a fixed, unit-based, or per-encounter methodology rather than actual Direct Service minutes.

The Compensation Schedule will identify the applicable:

  • service or billing code;
  • Direct Service value;
  • Direct Service minutes or time-equivalent;
  • Included Indirect Service allowance;
  • Direct Service calculation methodology;
  • Workload Clinical Hour Value;
  • and other applicable service-specific requirements.

Every fixed or per-encounter Integrated Service should maintain an underlying Direct Service time or time-equivalent for purposes of:

  • payroll administration;
  • Sick Leave calculations;
  • Excess Time review;
  • Minimum Workload calculations;
  • workload measurement; and
  • compensation auditing.

Unless otherwise specified:

Included Indirect Service = 20% of the assigned Direct Service time or time-equivalent.

An Integrated Service does not also generate FFS Clinical Hour compensation for the same service unless expressly authorized in the Compensation Schedule.

sections.title: 12. Routine Administrative Work Included in Integrated Services
sections.bodyHtml:
The Included Indirect Service Component is intended to compensate routine activities directly associated with the Integrated Service.

These may include:

  • routine documentation;
  • ordinary preparation;
  • routine chart review;
  • brief client or guardian communication;
  • brief authorized care coordination;
  • routine service-related scheduling;
  • brief follow-up;
  • routine documentation corrections; and
  • other ordinary administrative activities associated with completing the service.

Routine work already compensated through the Included Indirect Service Component is not separately compensated a second time.

sections.title: 13. Separately Compensated Indirect Service
sections.bodyHtml:
Indirect Service is an intentionally limited category of separately compensable work directly related to client care, completion of clinical services, or authorized client acquisition and coordination.

Because routine administrative work is already accounted for through either:

  • the FFS Clinical Hour methodology; or
  • the Included Indirect Service Component of an Integrated Service;
  • separate Indirect Service compensation is generally reserved for:
  • qualifying Excess Indirect Time;
  • clinically necessary work exceeding an applicable service allowance;
  • specifically authorized care coordination not incorporated into another service;
  • client or guardian communication not already compensated;
  • substantial chart review;
  • authorized client-acquisition activity;
  • approved outreach intended to identify, engage, or coordinate potential clients;
  • preparation directly associated with approved client outreach; and
  • other work expressly designated as qualifying Indirect Service.

An activity does not qualify as Indirect Service merely because it benefits the Practice or generally relates to the Employee's employment.

sections.title: 14. Support Activity
sections.bodyHtml:
Support Activity is separately compensable employment-related work that does not qualify as Direct Service or qualifying Indirect Service.

Support Activities include, as applicable:

  • onboarding;
  • orientation;
  • required training;
  • staff meetings;
  • team meetings;
  • huddles;
  • Town Halls;
  • Administrative Updates;
  • compensated supervision;
  • required supervision activities when compensation applies;
  • implementation meetings;
  • operational meetings;
  • required technology or systems training;
  • assigned internal administrative activities;
  • required professional development;
  • compensable travel to outreach activities;
  • compensable travel associated with other Practice assignments; and
  • other authorized organizational work outside Direct or qualifying Indirect Service.

Support Activity is compensated at the Employee's applicable Support Activity Rate.

Approved outreach activity directed toward client acquisition may qualify as Indirect Service.

Compensable travel associated with that outreach assignment is generally classified as Support Activity.

sections.title: 15. Excess Time
sections.bodyHtml:
Employees are not expected to perform separately compensable required work without compensation.

Excess Time exists when properly documented required work exceeds the amount reasonably compensated or contemplated by the applicable service structure.

A. FFS Excess Time

For FFS Clinical Hour Services, the Practice generally evaluates service-related work against the aggregate Standard Time Equivalent during the Employee's regular 14-day pay period.

For example:

20 Clinical Hours × 1.20 = 24 Standard Time Equivalent Hours

Normal variation between individual services is expected.

An individual service taking more time than its proportional Standard Time Equivalent does not automatically create additional separately payable time when other qualifying services reasonably balance the variation.

When properly documented required service-related work exceeds the aggregate Standard Time Equivalent, the Employee may submit the qualifying excess.

B. Integrated Service Excess Time

For Integrated Services, ordinary compensation includes:

  • the applicable Direct Service Component; and
  • the Included Indirect Service Component.

For Per-Minute Integrated Services, qualifying Direct Service minutes are already compensated based upon actual Direct Service minutes.

For fixed, unit-based, or per-encounter Integrated Services, the assigned Direct Service time or time-equivalent establishes the ordinary service allocation.

Where required Direct Service materially exceeds the amount already compensated by a fixed service allocation, qualifying additional Direct Service may be submitted where applicable.

Where required Indirect Service exceeds the Included Indirect Service allowance, the Employee may submit qualifying additional Indirect Service.

Normal variation may be evaluated over the applicable 14-day pay period.

sections.title: 16. Excess Time Compensation
sections.bodyHtml:
Direct Excess Time

Qualifying Direct Service not already compensated through the applicable service payment is compensated according to the applicable Direct Service or service-specific methodology.

For Integrated Services, approved additional Direct Service may also generate the corresponding ordinary Included Indirect Service allowance unless that administrative work has already been separately compensated.

Indirect Excess Time

Qualifying Indirect Service exceeding the amount already included in the applicable service compensation is compensated at the Employee's applicable Indirect Service Rate.

Only the amount exceeding the compensation or time allowance already incorporated into the service is separately payable.

sections.title: 17. Excess Time Documentation
sections.bodyHtml:
Excess Time must be timely and sufficiently documented.

The Employee should identify, as applicable:

  • the service or services involved;
  • date or dates;
  • additional amount of time;
  • whether the additional activity was Direct or Indirect;
  • general nature of the work performed; and
  • reason the applicable service allowance was exceeded.

Employees should avoid placing unnecessary protected health information into payroll records when the time can be verified through the clinical record.

The Practice may request reasonable clarification or supporting documentation.

Employees should obtain advance authorization for foreseeable non-routine activity when reasonably practicable.

Required compensable work must nevertheless be accurately reported.

sections.title: 18. Sick Leave Time Equivalency
sections.bodyHtml:
Service compensation and Sick Leave accrual are separate calculations.

FFS Clinical Hour Services

Unless otherwise specified:

1.00 Clinical Hour = 1.20 hours credited toward the Sick Leave accrual calculation

Examples:

Clinical HoursTime Credited Toward Sick Leave Accrual
0.500.60 hours
0.750.90 hours
1.001.20 hours
1.501.80 hours
10.0012.00 hours

These are hours credited toward the Sick Leave accrual calculation.

They are not the amount of Sick Leave earned.

Integrated Services

For Integrated Services:

Compensated Direct Service Time + Included Indirect Service Time = Standard Sick Leave Time Equivalent

Unless another allowance applies:

60 minutes Direct + 12 minutes Included Indirect = 72 minutes credited toward Sick Leave accrual

and:

15 minutes Direct + 3 minutes Included Indirect = 18 minutes credited toward Sick Leave accrual

Separately compensated qualifying time, including:

  • Indirect Service;
  • Support Activity;
  • Excess Direct Time;
  • Excess Indirect Time; and
  • other compensable work

will also be included as applicable.

The Practice will not reduce the standard Sick Leave time credit solely because an Employee completes routine service-related work more efficiently than the applicable standard allowance.

Sick Leave itself is administered according to the Practice's separate Sick Leave Policy and applicable law.

sections.title: 19. Workload Clinical Hours
sections.bodyHtml:
Clinical Hours may also be assigned for workload measurement even when the underlying service is compensated as an Integrated Service.

The Compensation Schedule may therefore assign a Workload Clinical Hour Value to:

  • FFS Clinical Hour Services;
  • Integrated Services;
  • Per-Minute Services;
  • unit-based services;
  • fixed services; and
  • other qualifying direct services.

Workload Clinical Hours may be used for:

  • minimum workload requirements;
  • tier determination;
  • productivity measurement;
  • caseload expectations; and
  • other operational purposes.

A service's Workload Clinical Hour Value and compensation method are separate.

A service may therefore count as 1.00 Workload Clinical Hour without being paid as 1.00 FFS Clinical Hour.

sections.title: 20. Minimum Workload Rate
sections.bodyHtml:
Effective November 13, 2026, eligibility for the applicable Standard Professional Rate requires at least:

12 Workload Clinical Hours during each standard 14-day pay period.

If the Employee completes fewer than 12 Workload Clinical Hours, the Practice provides one 14-day grace period.

If the Employee remains below the threshold after the grace period, the applicable Minimum Workload Rate begins prospectively with the following pay period.

The Minimum Workload Rate does not retroactively reduce compensation already earned.

FFS Services

For FFS Clinical Hour Services, the Minimum Workload Rate temporarily replaces the Employee's regular Clinical Hour Rate.

The service's Clinical Hour Value does not change.

Integrated Services

For Integrated Services, the Minimum Workload Rate temporarily replaces the applicable Standard Professional Rate used to calculate the Direct Service Component only.

The Employee's:

  • Indirect Service Rate;
  • Included Indirect percentage;
  • Support Activity Rate; and
  • separately approved Excess Indirect compensation

are not reduced solely because the Minimum Workload Rate applies.

sections.title: 21. Tier 3 Minimum Workload Exemption
sections.bodyHtml:
Effective November 13, 2026, an Employee who has achieved Tier 3 status during at least one of the preceding six completed pay periods is exempt from application of the Minimum Workload Rate solely because workload falls below the minimum threshold.

The exemption applies while the Employee continues to meet the applicable Tier 3 lookback requirement.

Tier calculations are governed by the Practice's applicable workload policies.

sections.title: 22. Denver Regional Differential
sections.bodyHtml:
Employees assigned to Practice-designated Denver regions may receive an additional Direct Service differential.

Unless another amount is expressly established:

Tier 2: +$1.00 per 1.00 Workload Clinical Hour

Tier 3: +$2.00 per 1.00 Workload Clinical Hour

The differential is prorated according to the Workload Clinical Hour Value assigned to the qualifying service.

The Denver differential applies to qualifying Direct Service only and does not increase the Employee's:

  • Indirect Service Rate;
  • Support Activity Rate; or
  • Included Indirect Service calculation.

sections.title: 23. Spanish Language Proficiency Differential
sections.bodyHtml:
The Spanish Language Proficiency Differential is intended to recognize Employees who have completed a Practice-approved Spanish-language proficiency program and demonstrated successful completion through an approved certificate.

Eligibility is not established solely by self-identification as bilingual, conversational ability, prior informal language use, or the Employee's assertion of proficiency.

To qualify, the Employee must satisfy the requirements below.

A. Approved Spanish Proficiency Course

The Employee must successfully complete a Spanish-language course, training program, or certification program that has been approved by the Practice in advance for purposes of the Spanish Language Proficiency Differential.

The Practice may maintain a list of approved programs within the Workplace Handbook, employee application, or other designated policy resource.

An Employee who wishes to use a course that is not already on the approved list must obtain Practice approval before enrolling if the Employee intends to seek reimbursement or qualification through that program.

Completion of an unapproved course does not automatically establish eligibility for the differential or reimbursement.

B. Successful Certificate Required

The Employee must successfully complete the approved course and obtain the applicable:

  • certificate of completion;
  • proficiency certificate;
  • credential; or
  • other completion documentation required by the approved program.

Attendance alone is insufficient.

The certificate or other required documentation must demonstrate successful completion of the approved program.

The Employee must submit acceptable documentation through the Practice's designated application or credentialing process.

C. Employee-Paid Course Cost

Unless the Practice expressly agrees otherwise in advance, the Employee is responsible for paying the initial cost of the approved Spanish proficiency course.

Course enrollment does not itself guarantee reimbursement.

D. Reimbursement After Probationary Period

Where the course is approved for reimbursement, the Practice will reimburse the eligible approved course cost after the Employee successfully completes the applicable probationary period and satisfies all required documentation requirements.

The standard probationary period is:

90 days

unless another probationary period is expressly established for the Employee.

To qualify for reimbursement, the Employee must:

  • have completed a Practice-approved course;
  • have obtained the required successful certificate or completion documentation;
  • submit proof of payment;
  • submit the required certificate or credential;
  • successfully complete the applicable probationary period; and
  • remain actively employed and otherwise eligible for reimbursement at the time reimbursement is processed.

The Practice may establish reasonable reimbursement limits, documentation requirements, and approved program costs through the applicable reimbursement policy or approved-course listing.

E. Effective Date of Differential

The Spanish Language Proficiency Differential begins prospectively after the Practice verifies and approves the Employee's qualifying certificate and updates the Employee's eligibility status in the application.

Completion of a course does not retroactively create a differential for services performed before the Employee's eligibility was verified and activated.

F. Qualifying Spanish-Language Services

The Spanish Language Proficiency Differential applies only to qualifying Direct Services in which the Employee's approved Spanish-language proficiency is actually required or utilized as designated by the Practice.

The differential does not automatically apply to every service performed by an Employee who holds the proficiency designation.

Eligible services must be identified through the applicable service record, client language designation, assignment, or other Practice-approved mechanism.

G. Differential Amount

Unless another amount is expressly established:

Tier 2: +$1.00 per 1.00 Workload Clinical Hour of qualifying Spanish-language Direct Service

Tier 3: +$2.00 per 1.00 Workload Clinical Hour of qualifying Spanish-language Direct Service

The differential is prorated according to the Workload Clinical Hour Value assigned to the qualifying service.

The Spanish Language Proficiency Differential applies to the qualifying Direct Service compensation and does not increase the Employee's:

  • Indirect Service Rate;
  • Support Activity Rate;
  • Included Indirect Service percentage; or
  • unrelated service compensation.

H. Continued Eligibility

Employees must maintain any documentation, certification, or continuing requirements associated with the approved proficiency program where applicable.

The Practice may suspend future differential eligibility when:

  • required qualification documentation expires;
  • the Employee no longer satisfies an applicable certification requirement;
  • the Employee is no longer assigned to qualifying Spanish-language services; or
  • another eligibility requirement is no longer satisfied.

Any change applies prospectively and does not reduce compensation already earned.

sections.title: 24. Introductory / Probationary Compensation
sections.bodyHtml:
Employees designated as subject to an introductory compensation period may receive an Introductory Professional Rate for the first 90 days of applicable employment or credential transition.

During the introductory period:

  • the Introductory Professional Rate may function as the Clinical Hour Rate for applicable FFS Services;
  • the Introductory Professional Rate may function as the Direct Service Calculation Rate for applicable Integrated Services;
  • the Employee's Indirect Service Rate remains separately established unless otherwise provided;
  • the Employee's Support Activity Rate remains separately established unless otherwise provided; and
  • ordinary Included Indirect Service calculations remain applicable.

An Introductory Rate and Minimum Workload Rate will not be stacked to create an additional reduction unless a prospective compensation provision expressly establishes that result.

sections.title: 25. Multiple Compensation Rates
sections.bodyHtml:
An Employee may receive multiple forms of compensation during the same pay period, including:

  • FFS Clinical Hour compensation;
  • Integrated Service compensation;
  • Indirect Service compensation;
  • Support Activity compensation;
  • Excess Time compensation;
  • regional differentials;
  • language differentials; and
  • other authorized payments.

Receiving more than one type of compensation does not convert an Employee's service-based compensation into a general hourly Direct Service arrangement.

The Practice will administer all compensation in accordance with applicable payroll and wage requirements.

sections.title: 26. Compensation Schedule
sections.bodyHtml:
The Practice maintains a separate Compensation Schedule identifying, as applicable:

  • service or billing code;
  • compensation method;
  • employee credential eligibility;
  • Clinical Hour Value;
  • Workload Clinical Hour Value;
  • Direct Service calculation rate applicability;
  • Direct Service minutes or time-equivalent;
  • Integrated Service calculation method;
  • per-minute treatment;
  • Included Indirect Service percentage or minutes;
  • applicable Indirect Service treatment;
  • regional or language differential eligibility;
  • service-specific restrictions; and
  • effective dates.

Employees should not infer compensation from a service's duration alone.

The Compensation Schedule applicable on the date the work is performed governs the service compensation.

Historical compensation rules will be retained for payroll and audit purposes.

sections.title: 27. Actual Work Time and Wage Compliance
sections.bodyHtml:
Clinical Hours, Workload Clinical Hours, Standard Time Equivalents, Integrated Service values, and actual work time are related but distinct concepts.

Clinical Hour

A standardized service-value unit used to determine FFS compensation.

Workload Clinical Hour

A standardized workload value used for productivity, tier, and minimum-workload measurement.

Standard Time Equivalent

The Practice's standardized time estimate associated with FFS Clinical Hour Services.

Integrated Service

A service-compensation method incorporating Direct Service compensation and an Included Indirect Service Component.

Actual Work Time

The compensable time the Employee actually spends performing work.

The Practice's service-based compensation methodologies do not eliminate applicable timekeeping, minimum-wage, overtime, Sick Leave, or other wage requirements.

Employees must accurately record or report compensable work as required by Practice procedure.

The Practice's 14-day Excess Time review methodology does not authorize averaging workweeks or days where applicable law requires a different calculation.

sections.title: 28. Employee Responsibilities
sections.bodyHtml:
Employees are responsible for:

  • accurately documenting qualifying services;
  • complying with billing and documentation requirements;
  • accurately documenting service duration when required;
  • completing documentation within required timelines;
  • using reasonable and efficient clinical and administrative workflows;
  • accurately reporting separately compensable Indirect Service;
  • accurately reporting Support Activities;
  • documenting qualifying Excess Time;
  • maintaining required credential and proficiency documentation;
  • accurately identifying qualifying Spanish-language services where applicable;
  • complying with internal payroll and application procedures; and
  • notifying the Practice when a recurring service or workflow consistently requires substantially more time than contemplated by the applicable compensation methodology.

The Practice may periodically review and prospectively revise Clinical Hour Values, Workload Clinical Hour Values, Standard Time Equivalents, Integrated Service methodologies, Included Indirect Service allowances, differential rules, and other compensation procedures to ensure that they continue to reasonably reflect service requirements, administrative demands, operational experience, payer requirements, and applicable law.

sections.title: Colorado Billing & Compensation Appendix
sections.bodyHtml:
Clinical Hour Rate currently covers approved 9-series clinical services at their assigned credit values. Standard Professional Rate currently covers approved H-code services at their documented hour or unit equivalents. Additional service codes may be assigned to either rate through a dated handbook update and an approved payroll mapping before use; a code prefix alone does not authorize a service or determine pay. Existing code-specific eligibility, indirect allowances and group restrictions continue to apply.

Clinical Hour Rate — approved 9-series services

Approved psychotherapy services, including 90832, 90834 and 90837, use the Clinical Hour Rate in the employee’s schedule. Family psychotherapy, psychotherapy add-ons, crisis services and group psychotherapy use their approved code-specific credit values and applicable authorization requirements. The “top” service rate is a category, not a promise of a full credit for every code. A 1.00-credit service pays the full credit rate; a 0.75-credit service pays 75% of that rate. No additional 20% indirect cash line is added to a clinical service-credit encounter.

Standard Professional Rate: H-code units and encounters in the app

Current app workflow. Payroll uses the services documented in the app. Use the employee’s applicable Standard Professional Rate and the code-specific basis below. A payer encounter is not automatically one hour of employee pay.

ServiceEmployee compensation basisDirect-pay formula
H0004 and other approved H-codes billed in 15-minute unitsVerified service units. One unit represents 0.25 compensation hour, even when actual service minutes differ.Units × 0.25 × applicable Standard Professional Rate.
H0031 and H0032, when billed per encounterActual documented service minutes, tabulated for payroll. The claim remains an encounter under the applicable payer rule.Documented service minutes ÷ 60 × applicable Standard Professional Rate.
Other H-codesThe approved code-specific mapping. Do not assume every H-code uses 15-minute units or that one encounter equals an hour.Use the dated mapping after billing/payroll verification.
Fifteen-minute unit boundaries

Where the applicable payer uses Colorado’s published 15-minute midpoint table: 8 through 22 minutes = 1 unit; 23 through 37 minutes = 2 units; 38 through 52 minutes = 3 units; 53 through 67 minutes = 4 units. Thus 23 minutes is two units, not one. Verify the payer, service-date rules, modifiers and authorized scope before billing; this compensation policy does not authorize a claim.

Included Indirect Service allowance

Integrated Services include Indirect Service time equal to 20% of compensated Direct Service time or its assigned time-equivalent, unless the Compensation Schedule expressly specifies another allowance. One direct hour includes 12 indirect minutes; 15 direct minutes include 3 indirect minutes. The included component is paid at the employee’s applicable Indirect Service Rate. Report qualifying excess work without duplicate payment.

Worked examples

At a $32 Standard Professional Rate and $22 Indirect Service Rate, one verified 15-minute compensation unit earns $8.00 direct and $1.10 included indirect; four units earn $32.00 direct and $4.40 included indirect. An encounter assigned 30 direct minutes earns $16.00 direct and $2.20 included indirect. Apply the service-specific Compensation Schedule and retain full precision until payroll aggregation.

Service-specific compensation method

The Compensation Schedule identifies whether each Integrated Service uses actual minutes, verified units, or a fixed encounter value. A software transition alone does not change the compensation method. Retain the method and effective date for each service date, including late-entered services.

Actual work and sick leave

Track actual direct, indirect and support work separately. Compensation units are not a substitute for actual-hours records. A service below a payer’s billing threshold or a delayed or denied claim does not erase pay for compensable work; report it for the appropriate payroll treatment. Payroll must reconcile minimum wage, overtime and other applicable wage requirements against actual work time. H-code direct compensation equivalents and paid indirect components enter the sick-leave calculation once; do not add the clinical-credit 1.20 multiplier. Reconcile against actual compensable hours and add any sick-leave accrual required by Colorado law.

Reference: Colorado behavioral health time documentation and unit rules. Billing must verify the current payer-specific requirements for the service date.

Actual time, payer units and internal credits

Record exact actual direct, indirect and support minutes separately from payer claim units and compensation credits. A qualifying 90837 maps to 1.00 compensation credit even when actual minutes differ from 60. Billing must follow the current payer’s requirements; a 53–74 minute example is not a universal maximum-duration rule. Verify scope, supervision, modifiers, place of service and telehealth rules for each service date. Never use leave-equivalent hours as actual hours worked.

Counseling service authorization

Inner Strength Institute provides counseling and the clinical assessment, treatment planning and coordination needed to support that care. Only services within the counseling practice’s approved scope may be scheduled or billed. A saved compensation mapping does not authorize another service line. Any client group remains subject to express written leadership approval before advertising, enrollment or scheduling, with verified provider, supervision and payer requirements.

Probation and transition

Probation is at most 90 calendar days from original start, ends on an earlier manual waiver or achievement of Tier 3, and never restarts after Tier 3. Probation uses the disclosed minimum-workload rate in each pay category. Minimum-workload reductions are waived for 60 calendar days after the amendment’s prospective effective date. An October 10 effective date is protected through December 8; the reduction can first apply December 9. The waiver does not restart or extend probation. Track service dates across every rate boundary.
